definition_zh: 改进；改善；提高
definition_en: to make something better, or to become better in quality, condition, or skill
core_image: 一块粗糙的木料被刨子一遍遍推过，表面一点点变平变亮
scene: 木工房里，老师傅推着刨子，一次一次从粗木板上削下薄薄一层。Keep practising and your handwriting will improve within a month.
sceneCN: 这里 improve 是「改进、变好」（第 1 个义项：质量或状况向好的方向变化），句意是坚持练习，一个月内你的字就会变好。画面里有木工房、刨子和一层层削下的木花。

pos.zh: 动词：改进、改善；提高（技能、产量）；好转

collocations.zh: 在……基础上更进一步、胜过

derivatives.zh: 有启发性的、使人进步的

senses.title: To make something better
senses.definition: to make a thing or a condition better than it was
senses.definitionCN: 把事物或状况变得比原来更好
senses.example: The council improved the drainage along the main road.
senses.exampleCN: 市政部门改善了主干道沿线的排水。
senses.why: Here the verb takes an object: someone acts on something and raises its quality.
senses.whyCN: 此时动词带宾语：有人对某物施加作用，把它的品质提高。

senses.title: To become better
senses.definition: to grow better by itself, as a skill, a health condition, or a result
senses.definitionCN: 技能、健康状况或结果自行变好
senses.example: Her reading improved a lot after a summer of daily practice.
senses.exampleCN: 坚持一个暑假的每日练习后，她的阅读进步了很多。
senses.why: With no object, the change happens to the subject, and English does not need a separate verb for it.
senses.whyCN: 不带宾语时，变化发生在主语身上，英语不需要另造动词。

senses.title: To do better than before
senses.definition: used with on to say a new attempt beats an earlier one
senses.definitionCN: 与 on 连用，表示新的尝试超过了旧的
senses.example: The second design improves on the first in every detail.
senses.exampleCN: 第二个设计在每个细节上都胜过第一个。
senses.why: Improve on marks comparison rather than repair, so the earlier version stays as a measure.
senses.whyCN: improve on 指向比较而非修补，旧的版本因此成了一根标尺。

intro.en: Improve began in French as a word about turning a profit, and only later became the general word for making better.
intro.cn: improve 最初是法语中关于「获利」的词，后来才成为泛指「变好」的词。

items.en: En prou was a phrase meaning into profit, used of land or trade that produced gain.
items.cn: 古法语的 en prou 意为「进入收益之中」，用于能产生利润的土地或买卖。

items.en: The verb emprouwer grew from it, meaning to turn to profit, to make land yield more.
items.cn: 动词 emprouwer 由此长成，意为「使之有利可图」，让土地多出产。

items.en: English borrowed it as improwen in the fifteenth century, first in farming and estate accounts.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入，写作 improwen，最初见于农事与庄园账目。

items.en: The sense widened from land to anything: a house could be improved, then a method, then a person.
items.cn: 词义从土地扩展到一切：房屋可以改善，方法可以改善，人也可以改善。

items.en: The spelling settled as improve, and the older money sense now survives only in the phrase improve the occasion.
items.cn: 拼写后来固定为 improve，较早的「获利」义如今只留在少数固定说法里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words beginning with the same im- shell; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs of getting better.
note.cn: 形近组收同样以 im- 开头的词；近义组收其他表示「变好」的动词。

entries.definition: To agree officially to something, a completely different act.
entries.definitionCN: 「批准、赞同」，与 improve 只差一个字母，意思毫不相干。

entries.definition: The noun for the change or the thing that was changed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词形式，指改进这件事或改进之处。

entries.definition: Better than before, used before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词作形容词，放在名词前表示「改良过的」。

entries.definition: To raise the value or appeal of something already good.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「提升、增强」，让本来就不错的东西更有价值。

entries.definition: To replace something with a better model or version.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「升级」，用更好的型号或版本替换。

entries.definition: To remove small faults by careful repeated work.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「精炼、打磨」，靠细致反复的工作去掉小毛病。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the farming origin of profit and the three patterns the verb takes with and without an object.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子利用它「获利」的农事出身，以及动词带宾语与不带宾语的几种句式。

normal.en: Improve began as a word for making land yield more, so better and more profitable still sit close together.
normal.cn: improve 起初是说让土地多出产，所以「更好」和「更有利」至今挨得很近。

normal.en: It works with or without an object: you improve a text, and the text improves.
normal.cn: 它既可带宾语也可不带：你改进一篇文章，文章也会变好。

normal.en: Improve on means beat, so the new version is not repairing the old one but beating it.
normal.cn: improve on 意思是胜过，新版本不是在修旧的，而是在赢过它。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with approve, which means giving permission for something.
normal.cn: 别与 approve 混淆，那个词是「批准」。

normal.en: The noun improvement keeps the -ment of result, so an improvement is the thing left after the work.
normal.cn: 名词 improvement 带 -ment 表示结果，所以改进之处就是干完活剩下的东西。

abstract.en: Improvement assumes a scale: nothing is better without a standard to be better than.
abstract.cn: 改进预设了一把尺子：没有可比的旧标准，就谈不上更好。

abstract.en: The word carries its commercial past, which is why improving land and improving profits sound so natural.
abstract.cn: 这个词扛着商业出身，所以「改良土地」和「提高利润」听来一样自然。

abstract.en: Small daily improvements compound, while grand rewrites often collapse.
abstract.cn: 每天的小改进会累积，而大改造常常垮掉。

examples.en: Reading aloud every day will improve your pronunciation.
examples.cn: 每天朗读会改善你的发音。

examples.en: The roads improved noticeably after the new budget passed.
examples.cn: 新预算通过后，路况明显好转。

examples.en: No one has improved on her record in twenty years.
examples.cn: 二十年来没人打破过她的纪录。

dict_mnemonic.text: im 进入 + prove 利益——让它进入更好的收益里，就是改进

root: 源自古法语 en prou「进入收益之中」及动词 emprouwer「使之有利可图」，十五世纪进入英语，最初用于农事与庄园账目，后泛指「改好、提高」，现代义已覆盖技能、状况与设计。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: making something better, becoming better by itself, and beating an earlier version.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：把某物改好，自身变好，以及在比较中胜过旧版本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plane shaving a rough board thinner and thinner until it shines.
core.cn: 核心意象：刨子一趟趟从粗木板上削下木花，直到板面发亮。

branches.en: THE HAND: with an object, improve is work done on something.
branches.cn: 动手线：带宾语时，improve 是对某物做的功夫。

branches.en: THE GROWTH: without an object, the change belongs to the subject.
branches.cn: 成长线：不带宾语时，变化归主语自己所有。

branches.en: THE COMPARISON: improve on ranks a new version above an old one.
branches.cn: 比较线：improve on 把新版本排在旧版本之上。

branches.en: THE FARM: the oldest sense made land yield more.
branches.cn: 农事线：最老的义项是让土地多出产。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: improvement and unimproved mark the result and its absence.
branches.cn: 词族线：improvement 与 unimproved 标出成果与未改进。

items.meaning: the change or the better part
items.example: The new roof is a real improvement.
items.exampleCN: 新屋顶确实是一大改进。

items.example: The improved engine uses less fuel.
items.exampleCN: 改进后的发动机更省油。

items.example: The talk was improving for the whole class.
items.exampleCN: 那场讲话对全班都有启发。

items.example: The unimproved meadow is full of wild flowers.
items.exampleCN: 那片未改良的草地里满是野花。

items.example: He proved the point with two examples.

definition_zh: 改进；改善；改进之处
definition_en: the act of making something better, or a change that makes something better than before
core_image: 同一段路前后对比：左边坑坑洼洼，右边新铺的柏油在阳光下泛光
scene: 村口那条土路修好之后，孩子们推着车跑得飞快，不再怕下雨天。Someone said the road had seen no improvement in twenty years.
sceneCN: 这里 improvement 是「改进、改善」（第 1 个义项：让情况变好的改变），句意是新排水系统是这些年来学校最大的一处改变。画面里有修好的村路、推车跑过的小孩和新铺的柏油。

pos.zh: 名词：改进、改善；改进之处；进步

senses.title: The act of making better
senses.definition: the process of making something better in quality or condition
senses.definitionCN: 使事物在质量或状况上变好的过程
senses.example: The improvement of the water supply took two years.
senses.exampleCN: 供水系统的改善花了两年时间。
senses.why: The -ment suffix names the action itself, so this sense is about the work rather than the result.
senses.whyCN: -ment 后缀指的是动作本身，所以这一义项说的是功夫，而不是结果。

senses.title: A change that makes things better
senses.definition: one particular change that makes a place, plan, or product better
senses.definitionCN: 某一处让地方、计划或产品变得更好的具体改动
senses.example: A second window was the only improvement the room needed.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间唯一需要改的就是再加一扇窗。
senses.why: From the process the noun turns countable and points to a single piece of work done.
senses.whyCN: 名词从过程变为可数，指向具体做成的某一处。

senses.title: Getting better in health or skill
senses.definition: the way a person's condition or ability gets better over time
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的状况或能力随时间变好的过程
senses.example: The doctor saw a slow improvement in his breathing.
senses.exampleCN: 医生看到他的呼吸在慢慢好转。
senses.why: The subject here is a person, so improvement describes recovery or growth rather than repair.
senses.whyCN: 这里的主语是人，所以 improvement 指的是康复或长进，而非修补。

intro.en: Improvement comes from the same French root as improve, which once meant turning something to profit.
intro.cn: improvement 与 improve 同源，都出自法语，原意是「使之有利可图」。

items.en: En prou meant into profit, and the verb emprouwer meant to make land yield more.
items.cn: 古法语 en prou 意为「进入收益」，动词 emprouwer 意为让土地多出产。

items.en: The noun formed on the same stem with the -ment ending that marks a result.
items.cn: 名词由同一词干加表示结果的 -ment 词尾构成。

items.en: English took it as improvement, first used for the work known as land improvement.
items.cn: 英语借入后写作 improvement，最初指今天仍称「土地改良」的那种活。

items.en: As the verb widened, the noun followed, covering buildings, methods, skills, and health.
items.cn: 随着动词义扩展，名词也跟着扩展，涵盖房屋、方法、技能与健康。

items.en: The plural improvements became the usual way to speak of separate works done to a place.
items.cn: 复数 improvements 成了指同一处地方所做的几项不同工程时的常用说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the improve family and its false friends; the near-meaning group gathers other nouns of progress.
note.cn: 形近组收 improve 一族词及易混词；近义组收其他表示「进步」的名词。

entries.definition: The verb that carries out the change.
entries.definitionCN: 动词形式，负责做出改变。

entries.definition: The same -ment ending on a different verb, meaning a shift of position.
entries.definitionCN: 同一 -ment 词尾接在另一个动词上，意为「移动」。

entries.definition: Official consent, from approve, which differs from improve by one letter.
entries.definitionCN: 「批准」，出自 approve，与 improve 只差一个字母。

entries.definition: Forward movement toward a goal over time.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「进展」，指朝着目标向前推进。

entries.definition: A change to a better model or a higher class.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「升级」，换成更好的型号或更高档次。

entries.definition: A planned change to a system that is thought to be faulty.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「改革」，针对被认为有缺陷的制度所做的改变。

normalIntro.en: The hooks work on the -ment result ending and on the fixed phrases that treat improvement as a countable gain.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子围绕表示结果的 -ment 词尾，以及把改进当成「可数收获」的固定搭配。

normal.en: Add -ment to improve and you get the thing done, just as a payment is the thing paid.
normal.cn: improve 加 -ment 得到「做成的结果」，就像 payment 是付出去的那笔钱。

normal.en: Room for improvement is the polite phrase for work still undone.
normal.cn: room for improvement 是委婉地说「还有活没干」。

normal.en: Make improvements to a place means leave it better than you found it.
normal.cn: make improvements to 一个地方，就是把那里弄得比来时更好。

normal.en: In medicine and sport, improvement is usually uncountable: a slow improvement, not an improvement of two.
normal.cn: 在医学和运动语境里，improvement 通常不可数，只说「慢慢好转」。

normal.en: Do not mix it with approval; one letter changes a better road into a signed form.
normal.cn: 别和 approval 搞混，差一个字母，路变好了就成了签字盖章。

abstract.en: The word once meant profit from land, and it still measures gain against what a place used to yield.
abstract.cn: 这个词原指从土地获利，如今仍在用「从前出产多少」来衡量增益。

abstract.en: Countable improvements are promises kept one by one, and they are what voters and patients actually feel.
abstract.cn: 可数的改进是一条条兑现的承诺，也是选民和病患真正感受到的东西。

abstract.en: Because it compares with the past, improvement can never be declared in the present tense alone.
abstract.cn: 因为它是和过去相比，所以改进不能只靠现在时来宣布。

examples.en: There has been a clear improvement in air quality this winter.
examples.cn: 今年冬天的空气质量有了明显改善。

examples.en: The essay is good but there is room for improvement in the last paragraph.
examples.cn: 这篇文章不错，不过最后一段还有改进余地。

examples.en: Watering the garden was the only improvement the new tenant asked for.
examples.cn: 给花园装浇水设备是新房客唯一提出的改进。

dict_mnemonic.text: improve 改进 + -ment 名词词尾——改进这件事或改进之处

root: 与 improve 同源，出自共同源于古法语的构词（en prou「进入收益」），名词形式先在英语中出现（improvement），最初指对土地与庄园所做的改良，后泛指建筑、方法、技能与健康方面的改善。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the work of making better, one particular better change, and a person's recovery or growth.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：改进这件事，某一处具体的改动，以及人在健康或技能上的好转。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two versions of the same road, one rutted and one freshly paved.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一条路的前后两版，一版坑洼，一版刚铺好柏油。

branches.en: THE WORK: improvement names the work done, often uncountable.
branches.cn: 工夫线：improvement 指所做的工夫，常为不可数。

branches.en: THE ITEM: made countable, it is one finished better thing.
branches.cn: 条目线：变成可数时，就是一处做好的改动。

branches.en: THE PERSON: for people it means recovery and growth.
branches.cn: 人身线：用在人身上，指康复与长进。

branches.en: THE PHRASE: room for improvement softens criticism.
branches.cn: 搭配线：room for improvement 把批评说软了。

branches.en: THE FARM: the land origin still shows in phrase like land improvement.
branches.cn: 农事线：改良土地这类说法里仍看得见它的出身。

intro.cn: 此表把表示结果的 -ment 名词与其来源动词放在一起比较。

latinIntro.en: The verb is Old French rather than Latin, though -ment itself came from Latin -mentum.
latinIntro.cn: 这个动词来自古法语而非拉丁语，但 -ment 本身出自拉丁语 -mentum。

A sudden movement scared the bird.

items.meaningCN: 名词：成就，同一 -ment 模式

items.example: The lessons had an improving effect.

items.meaning: one who or that which improves

items.exampleCN: 种植前会加土壤改良剂。

latinEntries.meaning: a suffix naming the result of an action
latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语后缀：表示动作的结果

latinEntries.meaning: to make better, the Latin cousin of the idea
latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语动词：使变好，表示同一概念的拉丁表亲

definition_zh: 冲动；突发的行动欲望；推动力；刺激；[物理] 冲量；[神经] 神经冲动；[电子] 脉冲
definition_en: a sudden urge to act, or a force that drives something forward
core_image: 一只手刚要伸向橱窗里的蛋糕，另一只手在手腕上轻轻按住
scene: 商场橱窗前，一个人原本只想路过，An impulse made him stop and buy the cake in the window.
sceneCN: 这里 impulse 指「突然想做某事的冲动」（第 1 个义项：突发的行动欲望）；句意为一股冲动让他停下来买橱窗里的蛋糕。图中可辨识物件：橱窗、蛋糕、购物袋、玻璃反光。

pos.zh: 冲动；突发的欲望；推动力；冲量；神经冲动；脉冲

senses.title: A sudden urge to act
senses.definition: a sudden strong wish to do something, often without planning
senses.definitionCN: 突然产生的强烈行动欲望，常未经计划
senses.example: She felt an impulse to laugh.
senses.exampleCN: 她突然想笑。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to drive against, so the urge arrives like a push from inside the body.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「朝前推」，因此冲动像从身体内部推来的一股力。

senses.title: A push or stimulus from outside
senses.titleCN: 来自外部的推动或刺激
senses.definition: a force or stimulus that drives something to move or respond
senses.definitionCN: 促使某物移动或作出反应的力量或刺激
senses.example: The first impulse came from the crowd outside.
senses.exampleCN: 最初的推动来自外面的人群。
senses.why: The push need not begin inside a person; any external force that starts a movement is an impulse.
senses.whyCN: 推力不必起于人的内部；任何引发运动的外力都是冲量意义上的推动。

senses.title: Force multiplied by time in physics
senses.titleCN: 物理中力与时间的乘积
senses.definition: in physics, the product of a force and the time during which it acts
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中，一个力与它作用时间的乘积
senses.example: The impulse changed the cart's momentum.
senses.exampleCN: 这个冲量改变了小车的动量。
senses.why: Physics measures a push by how long it lasts, so the word becomes a precise quantity.
senses.whyCN: 物理学用推力持续多久来度量推，于是这个词成了一个精确的量。

senses.title: A signal travelling along a nerve
senses.definition: a brief electrical change that travels along a nerve fibre
senses.definitionCN: 沿神经纤维传导的短暂电变化
senses.example: The nerve carries impulses from the finger to the spine.
senses.exampleCN: 神经把冲动从手指传到脊柱。
senses.why: A signal is a short burst of driving force, so physiology borrowed the same word.
senses.whyCN: 信号是一小段驱动力的爆发，因此生理学也借用了这个词。

senses.title: A short burst of signal in electronics
senses.titleCN: 电子学中的短促信号脉冲
senses.definition: a short sudden change in voltage or current, used to carry information
senses.definitionCN: 电压或电流的短促突变，用来承载信息
senses.example: Each key sends an impulse to the circuit.
senses.exampleCN: 每按一个键，都会向电路发出一个脉冲。
senses.why: The physical push shrinks to a brief burst, and the word follows it into circuitry.
senses.whyCN: 物理的推力缩小成一次短暂爆发，这个词便跟着进入电路。

senses.title: A purchase made without planning
senses.definition: a purchase made suddenly, without prior planning
senses.definitionCN: 没有事先计划、突然作出的购买
senses.example: The chocolates were an impulse at the checkout.
senses.exampleCN: 这些巧克力是结账时一时冲动买的。
senses.why: Commerce names the urge by its result, so the bought thing becomes an impulse.
senses.whyCN: 商业用结果来命名欲望，于是被买下的东西本身就成了「冲动」。

senses.title: The drive behind creative work
senses.definition: a strong inner drive that leads to creative work
senses.definitionCN: 促使人创作作品的强烈内在驱动
senses.example: He painted from an impulse rather than a plan.
senses.exampleCN: 他作画是凭一股冲动，而不是按计划。
senses.why: The surge that moves the hand can also move the brush, and art calls it an impulse.
senses.whyCN: 推动手的那股涌动也能推动画笔，艺术便称之为冲动。

senses.title: The drive behind behaviour
senses.definition: in psychology, an inner force that pushes a person toward action
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中，促使人行动的内在力量
senses.example: The therapist traced the impulse behind his spending.
senses.exampleCN: 治疗师追溯他消费行为背后的驱力。
senses.why: Psychology formalizes the push as a drive, keeping the physics of motion inside the mind.
senses.whyCN: 心理学把这股推力正式化为驱力，把运动的物理留在了心里。

intro.en: Impulse comes from Latin impulsus, a noun of action from impellere, to drive into or against. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: impulse 来自拉丁语 impulsus，是动词 impellere 的动名词，后者意为「推入、推向」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pellere meant to push or drive. Its older Indo-European source is reconstructed as a root meaning to thrust or strike, and that form is not recorded.
items.cn: pellere 意为「推、驱动」。它更早的印欧语来源被重构为一个表示「推、击」的词根，该词形没有记录。

items.en: In- meaning into plus pellere produced impellere, to drive into or against something.
items.cn: in-「进入」加 pellere 构成 impellere，意为「推入、撞向某物」。

items.en: The noun impulsus named a push or a shock, and classical Latin already used it for both physical and mental driving.
items.cn: 名词 impulsus 指推击或冲击，古典拉丁语已用它兼指物理与心理上的驱动。

items.en: English adopted impulse in the sixteenth century, first as a physical push and soon after as a sudden urge.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪引入 impulse，先指物理的推击，很快又指突然的欲望。

items.en: Physics, physiology and electronics each gave the word a precise technical sense from the nineteenth century onward.
items.cn: 物理学、生理学与电子学从十九世纪起各自赋予这个词一个精确的技术义。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English citation is not fixed, and the pre-Latin root of pellere is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 来源不确定：英语最早书证年代无定论；pellere 在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式，并非有记录的真实词。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb pellere but differs in prefix; the second holds words for urges and driving forces. One look-alike comes from a different root.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁动词 pellere，只是前缀不同；第二组是表示欲望与驱动力的词。有一个形似词来自不同词根。

entries.definition: To drive someone to act; it is the verb behind the noun impulse.
entries.definitionCN: 驱使某人行动；它正是名词 impulse 背后的动词。

entries.definition: Com- plus pellere: to drive together or force; it implies pressure that leaves little choice.
entries.definitionCN: com- 加 pellere：驱使到一处或强迫；它含几乎没有选择余地的压力。

entries.definition: Re- meaning back plus pellere: to drive away, as a surface drives off water.
entries.definitionCN: re-「向后」加 pellere：把东西推走，如同表面把水排开。

entries.definition: From Latin impetere, built on petere meaning to seek or attack, not pellere; it means momentum or driving force.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语 impetere，词根是 petere「寻求、攻击」而非 pellere；意为势头或推动力。

entries.definition: A strong desire to do something; impulse adds the note of suddenness and of arriving without planning.
entries.definitionCN: 想做某事的强烈愿望；impulse 多了「突然」与「未经计划」两层意思。

entries.definition: A continuing force that keeps someone working; an impulse is usually a short burst.
entries.definitionCN: 使人持续工作的力量；impulse 通常是短促的一次爆发。

entries.definition: Something external that causes a response; impulse can also name the inner wish.
entries.definitionCN: 引起反应的外在事物；impulse 也可以指内在的欲望。

entries.definition: The force of a body already moving; an impulse is what starts or changes that motion.
entries.definitionCN: 已经在运动的物体所具有的力；impulse 是启动或改变该运动的推击。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real prefix, the root of driving, the real family and the phrases the noun keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的前缀、表示「驱动」的词根、真实的同族词，以及这个名词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: in- meaning into plus pellere meaning drive: a push that enters and sets something moving.
normal.cn: in-「进入」加 pellere「驱动」：一股推进来，把东西带动起来。

normal.en: The family runs impulse, impel, impulsive, impulsively and impulsiveness.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 impulse（冲动）、impel（推动）、impulsive（冲动的）、impulsively（冲动地）、impulsiveness（冲动性）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: on impulse, impulse buying, resist an impulse, act on impulse.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：一时冲动、冲动购买、克制冲动、凭冲动行事。

normal.en: Physics measures impulse as force times time, which makes the everyday push exact.
normal.cn: 物理学把冲量度量成力乘时间，让日常的「推」变得精确。

normal.en: Impetus looks like impulse but comes from seeking, not driving, so the roots differ.
normal.cn: impetus 看似与 impulse 同族，却来自「寻求」而不是「驱动」，词根并不相同。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching for a cake and another hand holding the wrist.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸向蛋糕，另一只手按住了手腕。

abstract.en: Picture a short shove that sends a swing moving and then lets it coast.
abstract.cn: 想象一次短促的推，把秋千送出去，然后任它滑行。

abstract.en: Picture a spark crossing a gap for only a moment.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒火花只一瞬间穿过缝隙。

examples.en: He bought the guitar on impulse and never learned to play.
examples.cn: 他一时冲动买了那把吉他，却一直没学。

examples.en: Her first impulse was to deny everything.
examples.cn: 她的第一反应是把一切都否认掉。

examples.en: A nerve impulse travels faster than a spoken word can follow.
examples.cn: 神经冲动的传导比话语跟得上的速度还快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一木炮死」——一股劲突然推过来，人还没想就先动了 → impulse 冲动

root: 拉丁 impulsus「推击、冲击」来自 impellere = in-「进入」+ pellere「推、驱动」；pellere 更早的印欧语词根被重构为表示「推、击」的形式。英语 impulse 经法语进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one push: a surge inside a person, a force from outside, a measured quantity in physics, a signal in a nerve, a burst in a circuit, a sudden purchase, a creative drive and a psychological drive.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次推动展开：人体内的一股涌动、外部的一股力、物理学里可度量的量、神经里的信号、电路里的爆发、突如其来的购买、创作上的驱动，以及心理上的驱力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand reaching for a cake while another hand presses the wrist down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手已经伸向蛋糕，另一只手把它的手腕按下去。

branches.en: URGE AND PURCHASE: the wish arrives suddenly and is sometimes named by the thing it bought.
branches.cn: 欲望与购买：愿望突然到来，有时又被它所买下的东西命名。

branches.en: PUSH AND DRIVE: an outside stimulus and an inner drive are the same force seen from two sides.
branches.cn: 推力与驱力：外在刺激与内在驱动是同一股力从两边看。

branches.en: MEASURED BURST: physics turns the push into force over time, and electronics into a pulse.
branches.cn: 可度量的爆发：物理学把推力变成力乘时间，电子学把它变成脉冲。

branches.en: NERVE SIGNAL: the body carries the same burst along a fibre.
branches.cn: 神经信号：身体把同样的爆发沿纤维传下去。

branches.en: CREATIVE DRIVE: the surge that moves a hand can also move a brush.
branches.cn: 创作驱动：推动手的那股涌动，也能推动画笔。

intro.en: Impulse can be read from a Latin prefix and a verb of driving that also build a wide English family.
intro.cn: impulse 可以按一个拉丁前缀与一个表示「驱动」的动词逐段读出，两者还构成一大族英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin pellere gives impel, compel, expel, repel and propel through related forms; in- adds direction into something.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pellere 通过相关形态衍生 impel、compel、expel、repel 与 propel；in- 加上「进入某物」的方向。

items.example: The prefix also appears in inject and invade.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀也出现在 inject（注入）与 invade（侵入）里。

items.example: Its stem survives in propel and repel.
items.exampleCN: 它的词干留在 propel（推进）与 repel（击退）里。

items.meaning: a push, hence a sudden urge
items.meaningCN: 一推，因而指突然的冲动

items.meaning: the tendency to act on sudden urges
items.example: His impulsiveness cost him the job.
items.exampleCN: 他的冲动让他丢了工作。

derivatives.structure: impulse + -ive (tendency) → tending to follow a sudden push
impulsive + -ly (adverb) → in the manner of a sudden push
impulsive + -ness (quality) → the tendency to act on urges
in- into + pellere drive → to drive someone into action
com- strongly + pellere drive → to drive with force

definition_zh: 冲动的；凭一时冲动行事的；未经思索的；[物理] 由冲量引起的
definition_en: acting or done suddenly on a urge, without planning or thinking first
core_image: 话还没在脑子里排好队，嘴已经先张开了
scene: 会议桌上，那句反驳还没想清楚就说了出口，Her impulsive reply ended the discussion before it began.
sceneCN: 这里 impulsive 指「凭一时冲动、不加思索就行动的」（第 1 个义项：易凭冲动行事）；句意为她那句脱口而出的反驳让讨论还没开始就结束了。图中可辨识物件：会议桌、半举的手、翻开的笔记本、冷掉的咖啡。

pos.zh: 冲动的；不经思索的；由冲量引起的

forms.label: 名词（冲动性，心理学用语）

senses.title: Acting on a sudden urge
senses.definition: given to acting suddenly on a strong urge rather than after thought
senses.definitionCN: 惯于凭强烈欲望突然行动，而不是先思考
senses.example: He is impulsive and buys things he never uses.
senses.exampleCN: 他很冲动，常买些从不用到的东西。
senses.why: The adjective attaches the push of impulse to a person, so it describes a tendency rather than one act.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把 impulse 的推力附着在人身上，因此描述的是一种倾向，而不是一次行为。

senses.title: Done without planning
senses.definition: of an action, done suddenly without prior planning
senses.definitionCN: 指行为突然发生，事先没有计划
senses.example: Their move abroad was impulsive.
senses.exampleCN: 他们搬去国外是一时冲动。
senses.why: The same push can be attached to the act, and then the word judges the deed rather than the person.
senses.whyCN: 同一股推力也可以附着在行为上，于是这个词评价的是行为，而不是人。

senses.title: Blurted out in speech
senses.definition: of words, said suddenly before they have been considered
senses.definitionCN: 指话语未经考虑就突然说出
senses.example: It was an impulsive remark, and she apologized at once.
senses.exampleCN: 那是一句脱口而出的话，她马上道了歉。
senses.why: Speech can be pushed out as quickly as a hand can reach, so the adjective covers words too.
senses.whyCN: 话可以像手伸出去一样被推出来，因此这个形容词也涵盖言语。

senses.title: Produced by a sudden force in physics
senses.definition: in physics and engineering, caused by a short applied force
senses.definitionCN: 在物理与工程中，由短时施加的力造成
senses.example: The impulsive load bent the beam for a moment.
senses.exampleCN: 冲击载荷让横梁短暂弯曲。
senses.why: Technicians keep the original physical sense: a force that arrives in a short burst.
senses.whyCN: 技术人员保留了最初的物理义：以短促爆发形式到来的力。

senses.title: A trait studied in psychology
senses.titleCN: 心理学研究的冲动特质
senses.definition: in psychology, describing behaviour that responds to urges with little restraint
senses.definitionCN: 在心理学中，描述对欲望几乎不加克制就作出反应的行为
senses.example: The scale measures impulsive tendencies in children.
senses.exampleCN: 这个量表测量儿童的冲动倾向。
senses.why: A tendency can be measured, and the adjective becomes a clinical description.
senses.whyCN: 倾向可以被测量，这个形容词于是成了临床描述。

senses.title: Bought without planning
senses.definition: of a purchase, made on a sudden wish rather than a plan
senses.definitionCN: 指购买出于突然的欲望，而不是出于计划
senses.example: The impulsive purchase sat unused in the cupboard.
senses.exampleCN: 那件冲动买下的东西一直放在柜子里没用。
senses.why: Commerce applies the word to the object, and the deed becomes a label on the goods.
senses.whyCN: 商业把这个词用到物件上，行为于是变成了贴在货物上的标签。

senses.title: Energetic and ungoverned in style
senses.definition: of a style or performance, energetic and ungoverned
senses.definitionCN: 指风格或表演充满劲头、不受拘束
senses.example: The band played with an impulsive energy.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队演奏出一股不受拘束的劲头。
senses.why: Art values the push for its freshness, so the same word can become praise.
senses.whyCN: 艺术看重这种推力带来的新鲜感，因此同一个词也能变成称赞。

senses.title: Pushed rather than weighed
senses.titleCN: 被推着走而非称量过的
senses.definition: the abstract quality of being driven by a push rather than by deliberation
senses.definitionCN: 被推力带着走、而不是经过权衡的抽象性质
senses.example: The whole decision felt impulsive rather than reasoned.
senses.exampleCN: 整个决定感觉是被推着作出的，而不是推理出来的。
senses.why: The core contrast is between a push and a scale, and this sense states the contrast directly.
senses.whyCN: 核心对照就是「推力」与「天平」之间，这个义项直接把这层对照说出来。

intro.en: Impulsive is formed from impulse plus -ive, with a parallel Medieval Latin impulsivus. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: impulsive 由 impulse 加 -ive 构成，中世纪拉丁语中有并行的 impulsivus。年代均为约数。

items.en: The base noun impulsus named a push or shock, from impellere, to drive into.
items.cn: 基础名词 impulsus 指推击或冲击，来自表示「推入」的 impellere。

items.en: Scholastic and medical Latin used impulsivus for forces or movements that arrive as a sudden push.
items.cn: 经院与医学拉丁语用 impulsivus 指以突然推力到来的力或运动。

items.en: English adopted impulsive in the seventeenth century, first for physical pushes and soon for a person's sudden acts.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪引入 impulsive，先指物理上的推动，很快又指人的突然行为。

items.en: The nineteenth and twentieth centuries made the word a standard description of behaviour that follows urges without restraint.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪使这个词成为描述「不加克制就跟随欲望」的行为的标准用语。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English citation is not fixed, and the shift from physical pushes to human tendency is dated differently across reference works.
items.cn: 来源不确定：英语最早书证年代无定论；从物理推力转向人的倾向这一变化，各家参考资料给出的年代也不一致。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb pellere but differs in prefix; the second holds adjectives for hasty action. One look-alike comes from a different root.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁动词 pellere，只是前缀不同；第二组是表示仓促行动的形容词。有一个形似词来自不同词根。

entries.definition: The noun for the push itself; impulsive describes a person or act moved by it.
entries.definitionCN: 命名推力本身的名词；impulsive 描述被它推动的人或行为。

entries.definition: The tendency to act on impulses; impulsive is the adjective that names the same tendency.
entries.definitionCN: 凭冲动行事的倾向；impulsive 是命名同一倾向的形容词。

entries.definition: Com- plus pellere: driven by an inner compulsion that feels hard to resist; it is not the same as acting on a passing urge.
entries.definitionCN: com- 加 pellere：被一种难以抗拒的内在强迫驱使；与凭一时冲动行事并不相同。

entries.definition: From Latin impetere, built on petere meaning to seek or attack, not pellere; it means rash and forceful.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语 impetere，词根是 petere「寻求、攻击」而非 pellere；意为鲁莽而猛烈的。

entries.definition: Arising from one's own impulse without outside force; it can be warm and welcome, while impulsive often carries a warning.
entries.definitionCN: 出于自身意愿而非外力；它可以是温暖可人的，而 impulsive 常带警示意味。

entries.definition: Acting too quickly and without seeing the danger; it is more clearly critical than impulsive.
entries.definitionCN: 行动过快且没看到危险；比 impulsive 更明显地带有批评意味。

entries.definition: Done too quickly, often with poor results; it stresses speed, while impulsive stresses the inner push.
entries.definitionCN: 做得太快，常带来糟糕结果；它强调速度，impulsive 强调内在的推力。

entries.definition: Rushed forward with force and little thought; it adds violence of movement that impulsive need not have.
entries.definitionCN: 带着猛劲冲出去、很少思考；它多了动作上的猛烈，而 impulsive 未必有。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real noun base, the real adjective ending, the real family and the phrases the word keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的名词基础、真实的形容词词尾、真实的同族词，以及这个词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: impulse plus -ive: the ending turns a push into a tendency of a person or act.
normal.cn: impulse 加 -ive：这个词尾把一推之力变成人或行为的一种倾向。

normal.en: The family runs impulse, impulsively, impulsiveness and impulsivity.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 impulse（冲动）、impulsively（冲动地）、impulsiveness（冲动性）、impulsivity（冲动性，心理学用语）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: impulsive behaviour, impulsive decision, impulsive buy, impulsive spending.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：冲动行为、冲动的决定、冲动买下的东西、冲动消费。

normal.en: Compulsive shares the root but adds a prefix of forcing: it is pressure that will not let go, not a passing urge.
normal.cn: compulsive 共享词根，但加上了表「强迫」的前缀：那是甩不掉的压迫，不是一时的欲望。

normal.en: Impetuous looks like impulsive but comes from seeking, not driving, so the roots differ.
normal.cn: impetuous 看似与 impulsive 同族，却来自「寻求」而不是「驱动」，词根并不相同。

abstract.en: Picture a mouth opening before the sentence has been arranged.
abstract.cn: 想象句子还没排好，嘴已经先张开。

abstract.en: Picture a shopping basket filled before the list is read.
abstract.cn: 想象购物清单还没看，篮子已经装满了。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pushed forward by a spring it cannot see.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手被一根看不见的弹簧推向前。

examples.en: He tends to make impulsive decisions at the end of a long day.
examples.cn: 他在漫长的一天结束时容易作出冲动的决定。

examples.en: The letter was an impulsive response, written in anger.
examples.cn: 这封信是气头上的冲动回应。

examples.en: Engineers test how the bridge bears an impulsive load.
examples.cn: 工程师测试这座桥如何承受冲击载荷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一木跑媳妇」——没想清楚就先冲出去 → impulsive 冲动的

root: 由 impulse 加形容词词尾 -ive 构成；impulse 来自拉丁 impulsus，后者出自 impellere = in-「进入」+ pellere「推、驱动」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one push attached to a person: a tendency, an unplanned act, a blurted word, a sudden physical load, a measured trait, a purchase, an ungoverned style and the abstract contrast with deliberation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一股附着在人身上的推力展开：一种倾向、一次无计划的行为、一句脱口而出的话、一次突然的物理载荷、一种被测量的特质、一次购买、一种不受拘束的风格，以及与权衡相对的抽象性质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mouth that opens before the sentence inside it has been arranged.
core.cn: 核心意象：句子还没在脑中排好，嘴已经先张开了。

branches.en: PERSON AND TRAIT: a single sudden act hardens into a measurable tendency.
branches.cn: 人与特质：一次突然的行为会凝固成可测量的倾向。

branches.en: UNPLANNED DEED: the same lack of planning covers a journey and a purchase.
branches.cn: 无计划之举：同一种缺乏计划，既涵盖一趟远行，也涵盖一次购买。

branches.en: SPEECH: words are pushed out as directly as a hand reaches.
branches.cn: 言语：话语像手伸出去一样直接被推出。

branches.en: PHYSICAL LOAD: engineering keeps the original short burst of force.
branches.cn: 物理载荷：工程学保留了最初那股短促的力。

branches.en: STYLE AND CONTRAST: art may praise the push, while reasoning sets it against the scale.
branches.cn: 风格与对照：艺术可能称赞这股推力，推理则把它与天平对立起来。

intro.en: Impulsive is a noun base plus an adjective ending, and the base itself goes back to a prefix and a verb of driving.
intro.cn: impulsive 是一个名词基础加形容词词尾，而这个基础本身可追到前缀与表示「驱动」的动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin impellere gives impulse and impel, and the ending -ive, from Latin -ivus, turns the noun into a tendency; the same stock also gives compulsive and repulsive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 impellere 衍生 impulse 与 impel，来自拉丁语 -ivus 的词尾 -ive 把名词变成倾向；同一词干还衍生 compulsive 与 repulsive。

items.example: The prefix also appears in inject.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀也出现在 inject（注入）里。
它的词干留在 propel（推进）里。
这股冲动来得毫无预兆。

items.meaningCN: 被突然的推力带动；冲动的

items.meaning: the tendency to act on urges
items.exampleCN: 这种冲动倾向在这个家族里代代都有。

items.meaning: driven by a force that will not release
items.meaningCN: 被难以摆脱的力量驱使的
items.example: He had a compulsive need to check the lock.
items.exampleCN: 他有一种难以摆脱的检查门锁的需要。

items.meaningCN: 把人推开的；令人反感的

latinEntries.meaning: tending to; having the nature of

derivatives.structure: impulsive + -ly (adverb) → in the manner of a sudden push
impulsive + -ness (quality) → the state of following urges
impulsive + -ity (abstract noun) → the measurable trait of acting on urges
com- strongly + pellere drive + -ive → driven by an irresistible force
re- back + pellere drive + -ive → driving the observer away

definition_zh: 激励；刺激；奖励；诱因；激励性的
definition_en: something that encourages a person or organization to act, especially a reward or benefit, or an arrangement designed to produce such encouragement
core_image: 在前方放一块看得见的糖，让人愿意多走一步
scene: 这里指「激励」。 The manager points to the bonus table: We need an incentive that makes people want to finish early, not just one that punishes lateness.
sceneCN: 这里 incentive 是「激励、奖励」（第 1 个义项：促使行动的动力）；句意：我们需要一种让人愿意提前完成的激励，而不只是惩罚迟到的办法。图中可辨识物件：奖金表、白板、计时器。

pos.zh: 激励；奖励；诱因；刺激
激励的；起鼓励作用的（较旧用法）

forms.label: 比较级（名词性形容词，少用）

derivatives.zh: 激励化；以激励手段推动
激励（由 incentive 逆构，多为官方用语）

senses.title: Something that motivates action
senses.titleCN: 激励：促使人行动的东西
senses.definition: a thing that makes someone want to do something or work harder
senses.definitionCN: 使某人想要做某事或更努力的事物
senses.example: The chance to travel was a strong incentive to join the team.
senses.exampleCN: 有机会出差是加入这个团队的一大激励。
senses.why: Latin incentivus meant 'setting the tune'. The image is a musician striking up a melody that others then follow: the incentive starts the action, it does not push it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 incentivus 意为“定调、起调”。意象是一位乐手起了一个调子，其他人随之跟上：incentive 是启动行动，而不是推动行动。

senses.title: A money reward tied to performance
senses.titleCN: 金钱奖励：与表现挂钩的报酬
senses.definition: a bonus, commission, or payment offered for achieving a result
senses.definitionCN: 为达成结果而提供的奖金、佣金或报酬
senses.example: Sales staff receive an incentive for every contract they close.
senses.exampleCN: 销售人员每签下一份合同就能获得一笔奖励。
senses.why: The 'reward for harder work' sense entered general use in the mid-20th century through incentive payment and incentive scheme. The tune is now priced.
senses.whyCN: “为更努力工作而给的报酬”这一义项在 20 世纪中期经由 incentive payment 与 incentive scheme 进入通用语。此时“调子”被标上了价格。

senses.title: A tax or policy incentive
senses.definition: a government measure, such as a tax break, designed to encourage particular behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 政府为鼓励特定行为而设计的措施，如税收减免
senses.example: The tax incentive made solar panels cheaper for homeowners.
senses.exampleCN: 这项税收激励让家庭安装太阳能板更便宜。
senses.why: The state cannot order people to invest, so it places a benefit in front of them instead. The incentive is a tune the policy hopes people will dance to.
senses.whyCN: 国家不能命令人们投资，于是把一项好处放在他们面前。incentive 是政策希望人们随之起舞的那个调子。

senses.title: An economic signal
senses.titleCN: 经济信号：改变选择的诱因
senses.definition: in economics, a factor that changes the cost or benefit of a choice and therefore behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 经济学中改变某一选择成本或收益、从而改变行为的因素
senses.example: Higher prices create an incentive to use less fuel.
senses.exampleCN: 更高的价格形成了少用燃料的激励。
senses.why: Economists treat incentives as signals in a system of choices. A price is not an order, but it changes what people want to do next.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家把激励看作选择系统里的信号。价格不是命令，却改变了人们接下来想做什么。

senses.title: A spur to effort: the challenge itself
senses.titleCN: 激发干劲：挑战本身也是激励
senses.definition: anything that stimulates effort, including a difficult task, a prize, or a rival
senses.definitionCN: 任何激发努力的事物，包括困难任务、奖品或对手
senses.example: The rival team's speed was an incentive to train harder.
senses.exampleCN: 对手的速度成了更刻苦训练的动力。
senses.why: The motivating thing need not be pleasant or paid. A challenge sets a tune as effectively as a bonus, because it makes a better performance imaginable.
senses.whyCN: 激励之物不必令人愉快，也不必付费。挑战和奖金一样能定调，因为它让更好的表现变得可以想象。

senses.title: An incentive scheme or programme
senses.titleCN: 激励方案：制度化的奖励安排
senses.definition: an organized system of rewards used by an employer or organization
senses.definitionCN: 雇主或组织采用的有组织的奖励制度
senses.example: The company introduced an incentive scheme for safety suggestions.
senses.exampleCN: 公司为安全建议推出了一套激励方案。
senses.why: One incentive is a nudge; a scheme is a standing orchestra. The tune plays regularly so that behaviour keeps time with it.
senses.whyCN: 单个 incentive 是一次推动；scheme 则是一支常设乐队。调子定期奏响，使行为持续跟上节拍。

senses.title: A perceived benefit in decision-making
senses.titleCN: 被感知的好处：行为选择的依据
senses.definition: in behavioural economics, the benefit a person believes they will gain from an option
senses.definitionCN: 行为经济学中，一个人认为从某个选项中将获得的好处
senses.example: People respond to the incentive they perceive, not always the one intended.
senses.exampleCN: 人们回应的是自己所感知的激励，而不总是设计者所意图的那个。
senses.why: An incentive works only if it is seen. What matters is the benefit as the chooser imagines it, which is why the same reward can motivate one person and not another.
senses.whyCN: 激励只有被看见才起作用。关键是选择者想象中的好处，这正是同一份奖励能激励一个人却激励不了另一个人的原因。

senses.title: Adjective: inciting or encouraging
senses.titleCN: 形容词义：起激励作用的
senses.definition: in older use, serving to incite, excite, or encourage
senses.definitionCN: 较旧用法中，指起煽动、激发或鼓励作用的
senses.example: Milton used incentive in the sense of 'incendiary'.
senses.exampleCN: 弥尔顿曾用 incentive 表示“煽动性的”。
senses.why: The adjective came first in this branch, around 1600, and meant 'provocative, exciting'. It survives mostly inside the noun's modern sense of encouragement.
senses.whyCN: 这一支的形容词义约在 1600 年先行出现，意为“煽动性的、令人兴奋的”。它如今主要存留在名词“鼓励”这一现代义项里。

intro.en: Incentive is a Late Latin adjective turned noun. Its stated root is incinere 'to strike up, begin to sing', but the 'inciting' sense is generally thought to have been influenced by incendere 'to kindle'. The deeper PIE root *kan- 'to sing' is reconstructed, so the exact semantic path is marked as probable rather than certain.
intro.cn: incentive 是一个由晚期拉丁语形容词转来的名词。其明载词根是 incinere“起调、开始唱”，但“煽动”这一含义一般被认为是受了 incendere“点燃”的影响。更深的原始印欧语词根 *kan-“唱”属于重构，因此确切语义路径只能标为“一般认为”，而非确定。

items.en: First recorded as 'that which moves the mind or stirs the passion', from Late Latin incentivum, a noun use of the neuter adjective incentivus.
items.cn: 最早记录为“推动心智或激起情感之物”，来自晚期拉丁语 incentivum，即中性形容词 incentivus 的名词化用法。

items.en: Incentivus meant 'setting the tune', and in Late Latin 'inciting'. It came from the past-participle stem of incinere 'strike up, begin to sing'.
items.cn: incentivus 意为“定调的”，在晚期拉丁语中又指“煽动的”。它来自 incinere“起调、开始唱”的过去分词词干。

items.en: Incinere is in- 'in, into' + canere 'to sing', from PIE *kan- 'to sing'. A singer who begins sets the pitch that others follow, which is the core of the metaphor.
items.cn: incinere 是 in-“进入”+ canere“唱”，后者来自原始印欧语 *kan-“唱”。起唱的歌手定下音高，其他人跟随，这就是该比喻的核心。

items.en: The 'inciting' sense is generally thought to have been influenced in Late Latin by incendere 'to kindle'. That influence is described as apparent rather than proven, so this link is source uncertain.
items.cn: “煽动”义一般被认为在晚期拉丁语中受了 incendere“点燃”的影响。这种影响被描述为“似乎如此”，而非已证实，因此这一联系标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: The adjective is recorded with the sense 'provocative, exciting, encouraging'. Milton uses it in the stronger sense 'setting fire, incendiary'.
items.cn: 形容词被记录为“煽动性的、令人兴奋的、鼓励性的”。弥尔顿用过更强的“点火、煽动性”义。

items.en: Incentive as a system of rewards first appears in the jargon of the U.S. war economy in 1943; 'rewards meant to encourage harder work' is recorded from 1948, short for incentive payment.
items.cn: 作为奖励制度的 incentive 于 1943 年首先出现在美国战时经济用语中；“为鼓励更努力工作而给的报酬”这一义项自 1948 年有记录，是 incentive payment 的缩略。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the incent- shape; the near-meaning group separates the spur from the reward and the motive.
note.cn: 形近组共享 incent- 外形；近义组区分“刺激物”“报酬”与“内在动机”。

entries.definition: to use rewards to encourage behaviour. It is the verb built on incentive, common in business writing.
entries.definitionCN: 用奖励鼓励行为。它是建立在 incentive 上的动词，常见于商业写作。

entries.definition: something that discourages action. It is dis- 'opposite of' + incentive.
entries.definitionCN: 抑制行动的事物。它由 dis-“相反”+ incentive 构成。

entries.definition: designed to cause fires, or tending to stir conflict. It comes from incendere 'to kindle', the word that influenced incentive's meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 用于纵火的，或易于煽动冲突的。它来自 incendere“点燃”，正是影响 incentive 词义的那个词。

entries.definition: the reason or desire that makes someone act. It can be internal, while an incentive is usually an external offer.
entries.definitionCN: 促使人行动的理由或愿望。它可以是内在的，而 incentive 通常是外部提供之物。

entries.definition: something offered to persuade someone to act. It is close to incentive but sounds more like a lure.
entries.definitionCN: 为说服某人行动而提供之物。它接近 incentive，但更像“诱饵”。

entries.definition: something given in return for good behaviour or work. It is the concrete thing, while incentive is the reason the thing is offered.
entries.definitionCN: 因良好行为或工作而给予之物。它是具体的东西，而 incentive 是提供这份东西的理由。

entries.definition: something that causes a reaction or increased activity. It is broader and often biological or economic.
entries.definitionCN: 引起反应或增加活动的事物。它范围更广，常用于生物或经济语境。

normalIntro.en: Real roots and real terms; the key image is a musician striking up a tune.
normalIntro.cn: 真实词根与真实术语；关键意象是乐手起调。

normal.en: Latin incinere 'to strike up a song' gives incentive: the reward sets the tune others follow.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 incinere“起唱一首歌”给出 incentive：奖励定下调子，其他人跟着走。

normal.en: incentive, incentivize and disincentive share one stem; disincentive is the tune that makes people stop.
normal.cn: incentive、incentivize、disincentive 共享一个词干；disincentive 是让人停下的那个调子。

normal.en: A tax incentive is a benefit placed in front of a choice, not a command.
normal.cn: tax incentive 是放在选择面前的一项好处，而不是一道命令。

normal.en: An incentive scheme is a standing arrangement, while a single bonus is one note played once.
normal.cn: incentive scheme 是常设安排，而单笔奖金只奏响一个音符。

normal.en: In economics, incentives change the price of a choice, and people follow the changed price.
normal.cn: 经济学中，incentive 改变一个选择的“价格”，人们则跟随改变后的价格。

abstract.en: Picture a carrot on a stick held just ahead of a walker: the carrot does not push, it makes the next step worth taking.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绑在棍子上的胡萝卜，举在行人前方不远处：胡萝卜并不推人，它只是让下一步值得走。

abstract.en: An incentive is a tuning fork: it produces one clear note, and a whole group of actions fall into rhythm with it.
abstract.cn: incentive 是一把音叉：它发出一个清晰的音，一整组行动便随之落入节奏。

abstract.en: The same reward can be a gift or an insult, depending on who is listening to the tune.
abstract.cn: 同一份奖励可以是礼物，也可以是侮辱，取决于谁在听这个调子。

examples.en: Flexible hours are a stronger incentive than a small pay rise for many parents.
examples.cn: 对许多父母来说，弹性工时比小幅加薪更有吸引力。

examples.en: The subsidy was designed as an incentive to insulate old houses.
examples.cn: 这项补贴被设计为鼓励人们给老房子做隔热的激励。

examples.en: Without an incentive, the extra paperwork will simply not get done.
examples.cn: 没有激励，这些额外文书工作根本不会有人做。

dict_mnemonic.text: “硬森体武”——硬是精神抖擞地练武，因为有好奖励 → incentive 激励、奖励

root: 源自晚期拉丁语 incentivus“定调的、煽动的”，来自 incinere“起调、开始唱”，由 in-“进入”+ canere“唱”构成；核心是“先起一个调，让别人跟着动”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of incentive, all built on one image: something sets a tune and makes the next action worth taking. The tune may be money, policy, a rival, or a perceived benefit.
sensesIntro.cn: incentive 的八个义项都建立在同一个意象上：某物起了一个调，让下一步行动值得走。这个调可以是金钱、政策、对手，或一个人所感知的好处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clear note is struck ahead of the listener, and the listener's next move falls into step with it.
core.cn: 核心意象：在听者前方奏响一个清晰的音，听者的下一步便随之合拍。

branches.en: DRAWING FORWARD: a nudge, a challenge or a chance can start action without paying for it.
branches.cn: 向前牵引：一次推动、一个挑战或一个机会，不必付钱也能启动行动。

branches.en: PAID REWARD: the tune is priced and, in a scheme, played on a regular schedule.
branches.cn: 付费奖励：调子被标价；在方案中，它按固定日程反复奏响。

branches.en: POLICY AND MARKET: a tax break or a price change alters what behaviour is worth.
branches.cn: 政策与市场：税收优惠或价格变化改变某种行为的“值不值得”。

branches.en: PERCEPTION: only the benefit the chooser sees can move the chooser.
branches.cn: 感知：只有选择者看见的好处，才能推动选择者。

branches.en: INCITEMENT: the older adjective sense, where the tune is fiery rather than encouraging.
branches.cn: 煽动：较旧的形容词义，此时的调子是火热的，而非鼓励性的。

intro.en: Incentive is a complete Latin adjective, so English adds -ize, -ization and the negative prefix dis-. The internal in- belongs to Latin and cannot be removed.
intro.cn: incentive 是一个完整的拉丁形容词，因此英语只加 -ize、-ization 与否定前缀 dis-。内部的 in- 属于拉丁语，不可拆掉。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is canere 'to sing' and incinere 'to strike up'. Relatives include chant, canticle, incantation and the musical term cantata.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族是 canere“唱”与 incinere“起唱”。同族词包括 chant、canticle、incantation，以及音乐术语 cantata。

items.meaning: to encourage behaviour by offering rewards
items.meaningCN: 以奖励鼓励行为；使有动力（-ize 表示“使……化”）
items.example: The policy incentivizes companies to hire local workers.
items.exampleCN: 该政策激励企业雇用本地工人。

items.meaning: the act of making something reward-driven
items.meaningCN: 激励化；以奖励机制推动的过程
items.example: Incentivization of the sales team raised short-term numbers.
items.exampleCN: 对销售团队实行激励化提高了短期数字。

items.meaningCN: 抑制因素；反激励（dis- 表示相反）
items.example: High parking fees are a disincentive to driving downtown.
items.exampleCN: 高额停车费是抑制开车进市中心的因素。

items.meaning: to provide an incentive (official jargon, late 20c.)
items.meaningCN: 给予激励（由 incentive 逆构，20 世纪后期官方用语）
items.example: The scheme was designed to incent recycling.

items.exampleCN: 受激励的员工提交了更多申请。

items.example: The incentivized loan offered a lower rate for repairs.
items.exampleCN: 这项激励性贷款为维修提供较低利率。

items.meaning: organized around rewards rather than rules
items.example: They replaced fines with an incentive-based system.
items.exampleCN: 他们用奖励制取代了罚款制。

items.meaning: designed so that individual self-interest supports the intended outcome
items.meaningCN: 激励相容的（设计使个人利益与预期结果一致）
items.example: The auction was incentive-compatible for bidders.
items.exampleCN: 这场拍卖对竞拍者是激励相容的。

latinEntries.meaning: to strike up, begin to sing

definition_zh: 事件；事故；（不严重的）插曲
definition_en: something that happens, especially something unusual or unpleasant, or a single small event inside a larger one
core_image: 街角的路灯下，一只打翻的牛奶瓶和一地碎玻璃被警用黄带围了起来
scene: 清晨街角的路灯下，一只牛奶瓶翻倒在地，碎玻璃散了一小片。The police wrote down every detail of the incident before the street filled up.
sceneCN: 这里 incident 是「事件、事故」（第 1 个义项：发生的、多带负面意味的事情），句意是警察在街上人多起来之前记下了这起事件的所有细节。画面里有路灯、打翻的牛奶瓶和一小片碎玻璃。

pos.zh: 名词：事件、事故；（较大的事情中的）一件小事、插曲

collocations.phrase: at the scene of the incident

senses.title: Something that happens
senses.definition: an event, especially one that is unusual, unpleasant, or worth reporting
senses.definitionCN: 一件事情，尤指不寻常的、不愉快的或值得上报的事
senses.example: The school recorded three similar incidents last term.
senses.exampleCN: 学校上学期记录了三起类似事件。
senses.why: The word names a happening in the world, and English uses it most for things that disturb the normal order.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指世上发生的某件事，而英语最常用它来说打破常态的事情。

senses.title: A small episode inside a larger one
senses.definition: one small event that forms part of a longer story, journey, or process
senses.definitionCN: 构成一段较长经历、旅程或过程的一件小事
senses.example: The lost ticket was a minor incident in an otherwise calm journey.
senses.exampleCN: 丢车票只是这趟平顺旅程中的一个小插曲。
senses.why: Here the word orders events inside a narrative rather than warning of trouble.
senses.whyCN: 此时这个词是在叙述里给事件排位置，而不是警示有麻烦。

senses.title: An accident or clash
senses.definition: an accident, a fight, or a clash between groups, as reported by officials
senses.definitionCN: 官方通报中的意外事故、打斗或群体冲突
senses.example: A border incident nearly led to talks breaking down.
senses.exampleCN: 一起边境冲突差点让谈判破裂。
senses.why: Official language fixed the word on accidents and clashes, especially in police and military reports.
senses.whyCN: 官方语言把这个词固定在事故与冲突上，尤其在警务与军事报告中。

intro.en: Incident comes from a Latin verb for falling upon, and the idea of something that falls into your path still shapes it.
intro.cn: incident 出自拉丁语中表示「落在上面」的动词，而「落到你路上来的东西」这一意象至今仍在起作用。

items.en: Cadere meant to fall, and it underlies English words from accident to cadence and chance.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cadere 意为「落下」，accident、cadence、chance 都从它而来。

items.en: Incidere added the prefix in and meant to fall upon, as events fall upon a person.
items.cn: incidere 加前缀 in，意为「落在上面」，就像事情落在一个人身上。

items.en: The participle incidens was used as a noun for a happening, a thing that falls upon us.
items.cn: 分词 incidens 被用作名词，指落在我们身上的一件事。

items.en: French formed incident with the same sense of an event, often an unlucky one.
items.cn: 法语造出 incident，同样指一件事，且多指不走运的事。

items.en: English took it in the fifteenth century, and reporting language made it the standard word for accidents and clashes.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入，通报语言又把它定成事故与冲突的标准用词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same falling root; the near-meaning group gathers other words for happenings.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「落下」词根下的词；近义组收其他表示「事情」的词。

entries.definition: An unexpected harm nobody intended, from the same Latin verb with a different prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 「意外、事故」，同一词根不同前缀，强调无人故意。

entries.definition: How often something occurs across a group or a period.
entries.definitionCN: 「发生率」，讲的是频次而不是单件事。

entries.definition: By the way; used to add a side remark.
entries.definitionCN: 副词「顺便说一下」，用来补一句旁枝的话。

entries.definition: Anything that happens, usually planned or at least neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「事件」，中性，常指安排好的事情。

entries.definition: One part of a longer story or illness.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「一段插曲」，是较长故事或病程中的一节。

entries.definition: A fact of something happening, often noted in statistics.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「发生的事」，多见于统计与记录。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the falling image behind the root and the fixed phrases of official reports.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子利用词根背后「落下」的意象，以及通报中的固定搭配。

normal.en: An incident is something that falls on you; accident is the same fall with a different prefix.
normal.cn: incident 是落到你身上的事；accident 是同一种「落」，只是前缀不同。

normal.en: Without incident is the phrase for a journey that went exactly as planned.
normal.cn: without incident 形容一趟完全按计划走完的行程。

normal.en: Police write incident reports, which is why the word so often means something bad.
normal.cn: 警察写的是 incident report，所以这个词多半指不好的事。

normal.en: Incidentally means by the way, so a side event turned into a formula for changing subject.
normal.cn: incidentally 意为「顺便一提」，一件旁枝之事变成了改话题的套话。

normal.en: Keep the pair straight: an incident is one case, incidence is how often it happens.
normal.cn: 记住这一对：incident 是一件事，incidence 是发生的频率。

abstract.en: Naming something an incident is already a judgement that it is small enough to be handled.
abstract.cn: 把一件事称作 incident，本身就是在判断它小到可以处理。

abstract.en: The word carries a fall inside it, so every incident carries a hint of things going out of control.
abstract.cn: 这个词体内装着「落下」，所以每起事件都暗示着事物失去控制。

abstract.en: Reports choose the noun, and the noun sets the size: an incident rarely becomes a crisis on paper.
abstract.cn: 报告在挑选名词，名词也在设定大小：在纸上，事件很少升级为危机。

examples.en: The flight landed without incident despite the storm.
examples.cn: 尽管有暴风雨，航班还是平安落地。

examples.en: Teachers must report any incident involving a fight.
examples.cn: 任何涉及打斗的事件，教师都必须上报。

examples.en: The broken window was a small incident in an otherwise quiet term.
examples.cn: 这扇窗户被打破，只算是本该平静的一学期中的小插曲。

dict_mnemonic.text: in 在上 + cid 落 + -ent 名词词尾——落到你头上的一件事，就是事件

root: 拉丁语 incidere「落在上面」（in「在上」+ cadere「落下」）的分词 incidens 作名词，经法语 incident 于十五世纪进入英语；先泛指发生之事，后经警务与军事通报固定为「事故、冲突事件」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: an event worth reporting, a small episode in a larger story, and an accident or clash in official language.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：值得上报的事件，长故事里的小插曲，以及官方用语中的事故与冲突。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spilled milk bottle and a ring of glass under a street lamp in the morning.
core.cn: 核心意象：清晨路灯下，一只打翻的牛奶瓶和一圈碎玻璃。

branches.en: THE EVENT: incident names a happening that draws notice.
branches.cn: 事件线：incident 指一件引人注意的事。

branches.en: THE EPISODE: inside a story it marks one small chapter.
branches.cn: 插曲线：放在故事里，它标明一个很小的章节。

branches.en: THE REPORT: police and army language fixed it on accidents and clashes.
branches.cn: 通报线：警务与军事语言把它固定在事故与冲突上。

branches.en: THE PHRASE: without incident means all went as planned.
branches.cn: 搭配线：without incident 表示一切如常。

branches.en: THE PAIR: incidence measures how many times such events occur.
branches.cn: 对照线：incidence 量的是这类事件出现的次数。

intro.en: The table gathers words built on the Latin root cadere, to fall.
intro.cn: 此表汇集以拉丁词根 cadere「落下」为底的词。

latinIntro.en: Cadere with different prefixes produces accident, incident, occasion and decay.
latinIntro.cn: cadere 配上不同前缀，就有了 accident、incident、occasion 与 decay。

items.example: One small incident changed the mood.
Incidentally, the shop closes early today.
items.exampleCN: 顺便说一下，今天店关得早。

items.example: The incidence of the disease has doubled.
items.exampleCN: 这种病的发生率翻了一倍。

items.meaning: a particular time when something happens
items.example: It is an occasion worth remembering.
items.exampleCN: 这是个值得记住的场合。

items.meaning: to fall at the same point
items.example: The two holidays coincide this year.
items.exampleCN: 今年两个节日碰在一起。

items.example: The timbers decayed in the damp.

latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语分词：落在上面，引申为发生的事

definition_zh: 倾向；意愿；倾斜；倾角；斜坡
definition_en: a feeling of wanting to do something, or the angle at which something leans away from the level
core_image: 一根长杆原本立得笔直，有人从顶端轻轻一推，它便朝草地的方向偏过去，停在一个既不直立也不倒下的角度
scene: 院子里两张椅子并排放着，一张在树阴下，一张在阳光下，主人几乎没有停顿就坐进了有太阳的那张。His inclination was to stay in the garden rather than drive to town.
sceneCN: 这里本词指做某事的意愿倾向（第 1 个义项：心里更愿意选择的那一边）；句意为他的意愿是留在花园里，而不是开车进城。

pos.zh: 倾向；意愿（可数）
倾斜；斜度（可数）
倾角（天文学、物理学用语）

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀，回到同族动词，语义偏移为「使倾斜；倾斜」
由动词加过去分词后缀构成，语义偏移为「倾向于……的；倾斜的」
由动词加表「可……的」后缀构成，语义偏移为「易受影响而首肯的」
由动词词干加表测量仪器的成分构成，语义偏移为「测斜仪」
由本词加表角度的名词构成，语义偏移为「倾角」

senses.title: A leaning of the mind
senses.definition: a feeling that makes someone want to choose one course rather than another
senses.definitionCN: 使人更愿意选择某一做法而非另一做法的心理状态
senses.example: His inclination was to stay in the garden rather than drive to town.
senses.exampleCN: 他的意愿是留在花园里，而不是开车进城。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to bend something; the mind bending toward a choice kept the same picture.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词本义是使某物弯曲；心思朝某个选择弯过去，沿用了同一幅画面。

senses.title: The act of leaning
senses.definition: the movement or position of something that leans away from upright
senses.definitionCN: 某物离开直立状态而偏斜的动作或姿态
senses.example: A slow inclination of the mast told the crew the wind had shifted.
senses.exampleCN: 桅杆缓缓倾斜，船员便知道风向变了。
senses.why: The physical sense is the oldest one: a body that is no longer upright has bent away from the vertical.
senses.whyCN: 物理义最古老：一个不再直立的东西，就是从竖直方向弯开了。

senses.title: The size of that lean
senses.definition: the amount by which a line or surface deviates from the horizontal or vertical
senses.definitionCN: 直线或平面偏离水平或竖直的幅度
senses.example: The wall shows an inclination of four degrees from the vertical.
senses.exampleCN: 这堵墙与竖直方向有约四度的倾斜。
senses.why: Once the leaning was measured, the measurement itself took the same name.
senses.whyCN: 倾斜一旦可以测量，这个量本身也用了同一个名字。

senses.title: The tilt of an orbit
senses.definition: the angle between the plane of an orbit and a reference plane
senses.definitionCN: 轨道平面与某一参考平面之间的夹角
senses.example: Pluto's orbital inclination is far larger than that of the inner planets.
senses.exampleCN: 冥王星的轨道倾角远大于内行星。
senses.why: Astronomers borrowed the leaning image for a path that is tilted against the sky's flat plane.
senses.whyCN: 天文学家借「倾斜」这一意象，表示相对天空中那个平面而偏斜的路径。

senses.title: The dip of a magnetic needle
senses.definition: the angle at which a compass needle dips toward the earth's surface
senses.definitionCN: 指南针指针向下倾入地表的角度
senses.example: Sailors once measured magnetic inclination to guess how far north they were.
senses.exampleCN: 水手曾测量磁倾角来推估自己北行的距离。
senses.why: A needle that dips is a small bar of metal behaving like any leaning object, so the verb's image fits exactly.
senses.whyCN: 指针下倾，就是一小根金属像任何倾斜物体那样偏斜，动词的意象正好合用。

senses.title: A nod of the head
senses.titleCN: 点头或俯身的轻微动作
senses.definition: a slight bending of the head or upper body as a greeting or sign
senses.definitionCN: 作为招呼或示意而微微低头或俯身
senses.example: He answered with the smallest inclination of his head.
senses.exampleCN: 他只以极轻微的一点头作答。
senses.why: Bending the body forward is the literal old gesture, and courtesy still borrows it.
senses.whyCN: 身体前弯是字面意义上的古老动作，礼节的表达至今仍在借用它。

senses.title: A natural liking
senses.definition: a natural attraction to a particular activity, subject or kind of person
senses.definitionCN: 对某种活动、学科或某类人天生的亲近感
senses.example: She showed an early inclination for languages.
senses.exampleCN: 她早年就显露出对语言的爱好。
senses.why: A liking is the mind leaning without being pushed, so the word names what comes by itself.
senses.whyCN: 爱好是心思自己在弯，不用外力推，因此这个词指自发而来者。

senses.title: A slope in the land
senses.definition: a downward slope of ground, or the degree to which it falls away
senses.definitionCN: 地面向下倾斜的状态或落差程度
senses.example: The orchard sits on a gentle inclination facing south.
senses.exampleCN: 果园坐落在朝南的缓和坡上。
senses.why: Ground that leans is described with the same noun as a mind that leans, and the two images are the same one.
senses.whyCN: 地会倾斜，心也会倾斜，两者用的是同一个名词，本源也是一幅画面。

intro.en: Inclination comes from Latin inclinatio 'a leaning', built on inclinare 'to bend, cause to lean', itself in- plus clinare 'to bend'; the mental sense grew out of the physical one.
intro.cn: 本词来自拉丁语 inclinatio「倾斜」，其动词 inclinare 意为「使弯、使倾」，由表「向内」的前缀加 clinare「弯」构成；心理义是从物理义长出来的。

items.en: Clinare meant 'to bend, to cause to lean', a verb of the physical world rather than of feeling.
items.cn: clinare 意为「弯、使倾」，是物理世界的动词，而非情感的词。

items.en: Latin in- added direction, so inclinare meant 'to bend towards', to lean something in a given direction.
items.cn: 拉丁语表方向的前缀加在其前，构成「朝某方向弯」的动词，意为把某物往某一侧倾。

items.en: Inclinatio named the state or act of leaning, and could already describe a leaning of the will.
items.cn: 名词形式指倾斜的状态或动作，当时已可用来描述意志的偏向。

items.en: French passed the word to English in the fourteenth century, first as a physical and then as a mental leaning.
items.cn: 法语在十四世纪把该词传给英语，先指物理倾斜，再指心理倾向。

items.en: Astronomy and geomagnetism took the noun for the tilt of an orbit and the dip of a needle.
items.cn: 天文学与地磁学取用该名词，分别指轨道倾斜与指针下倾。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper root): the first English use is dated to the fourteenth century, while the older base behind clinare is generally considered a reconstruction, not an attested form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：英语首见书证定于十四世纪，而 clinare 背后的更早词基一般认为是重构形式，并非已见形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms that look close to this word and are often confused with it; group two holds words for wanting, leaning and liking that differ in force.
note.cn: 第一组是与本词形近、常被混用的形式；第二组是表示意愿、倾斜与喜爱的近义词，力度各不相同。

entries.definition: The past participle used as an adjective; it describes a person or thing that leans, while the noun names the lean itself.
entries.definitionCN: 由同一动词的过去分词转成的形容词，描述会倾的人或物；本词则是命名倾斜本身的名词。

entries.definition: A fixed compound naming the measured angle; the single noun names the leaning in general.
entries.definitionCN: 由两个词构成的固定组合，指被测出的角度；单个名词则泛指倾斜这件事。

entries.definition: An instrument for measuring a slope; it shares the leaning stem but ends in a device suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 测量坡度的仪器；与本词同出「倾斜」词干，但结尾是表仪器的成分。

entries.definition: An adjective for someone easily persuaded; it describes a person, while the noun describes the leaning itself.
entries.definitionCN: 形容容易被说动的形容词；描述的是人，本词描述的是倾斜本身。

entries.definition: A general direction in which something usually moves or behaves, often observed over many cases.
entries.definitionCN: 事物通常朝之发展或表现的方向，多由许多事例观察得出。

entries.definition: The everyday word for a preference or a physical tilt, closer to speech than the Latin noun.
entries.definitionCN: 表示偏好或物理倾斜的日常词，比这个拉丁名词更口语。

entries.definition: A liking for one thing over another after comparison, sharper than a mere inclination.
entries.definitionCN: 比较之后更喜欢某物，比单纯的倾向更明确。

entries.definition: A slope or a way of presenting something that favours one side, both physical and editorial.
entries.definitionCN: 坡度，也指带偏向的呈现方式，兼有物理与立场两层。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Two real parts: a prefix meaning towards, and a verb meaning to bend.
normal.cn: 两个真实成分：一个表「朝向」的前缀，加一个表「弯」的动词。

normal.en: The family runs incline, inclined, inclination, inclinable, inclinometer.
normal.cn: 同族词包括使倾斜、倾向于、倾向、易被说动的、测斜仪。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: an inclination to do something, follow one's inclination, magnetic inclination.
normal.cn: 固定说法：做某事的倾向、随自己的意愿、磁倾角。

normal.en: Every technical sense measures the same thing: how far a line, a path or a needle has bent from the level.
normal.cn: 每个技术义量的都是同一件事：一条线、一条路径或一根指针偏离水平多少。

normal.en: The mental sense is the physical sense moved inward: the will leans before the body does.
normal.cn: 心理义是物理义向内移的结果：意志先于身体倾过去。

abstract.en: Picture a straight pole pushed at the top until it rests at an angle, neither standing nor fallen.
abstract.cn: 想象一根直杆在顶端被推，直到停在一个斜角上，既没立着也没倒下。

abstract.en: Picture a needle in a glass case dipping its painted end toward the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃盒里的一根指针，带漆的一端朝地面下垂。

abstract.en: Picture a mind that leans toward one door before any argument is spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗心在还没听到任何理由之前，就已经朝某一扇门偏过去。

examples.en: She has an inclination to argue with every plan.
examples.cn: 她有一种对每个方案都要争辩的倾向。

examples.en: The tower's inclination has been measured for a century.
examples.cn: 这座塔的倾斜已被测量了一个世纪。

examples.en: Follow your inclination and take the longer path.
examples.cn: 随你的意愿走那条更长的路吧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把「朝向」与「弯」两部分合起来看：朝一边弯过去，就是倾斜，也是心思的倾向。

root: 拉丁 inclinatio「倾斜」，出自 inclinare「使弯、使倾」＝表「朝向」的前缀＋clinare「弯」；心理义由物理义引申，更深词基一般认为是重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one bend: a mind bends toward a choice, a mast bends from upright, the bend is measured, an orbit is tilted, a needle dips, a head bows, a liking forms, ground falls away.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「弯」展开：心朝选择弯去、桅杆离开竖直弯去、弯曲被测量、轨道被倾斜、指针下倾、头低下去、爱好形成、地面斜下去。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pole pushed at the top, resting at an angle between standing and falling.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根在顶端被推过的杆，停在一个既非直立也非倒下的斜角上。

branches.en: INWARD LEANING: a mind bending toward a choice and toward a subject are the same bend seen once and repeated.
branches.cn: 向内的弯：心朝某个选择弯去，与朝某门学问弯去，是同一种弯的一次与多次。

branches.en: THE BEND AND ITS SIZE: the leaning of a body and the measured amount of that leaning.
branches.cn: 弯与其量：物体倾过去，以及这个倾斜被量出的数值。

branches.en: SKY AND NEEDLE: an orbit tilted against a plane and a compass needle dipped by the earth.
branches.cn: 天与针：轨道相对平面偏斜，罗盘针被大地吸得下垂。

branches.en: THE BODY'S OWN BEND: a head or waist lowered in greeting is the oldest literal use.
branches.cn: 身体自身的弯：低头或俯身致意，是最古老的字面用法。

branches.en: GROUND THAT LEANS: a slope in land carries the noun back to the physical world.
branches.cn: 会倾的地：地面的坡度把这名词又带回物理世界。

intro.en: Inclination is a Latin noun built from a prefix, a bending verb and a noun suffix, and the same three parts reappear in English relatives, so the word can be read in pieces.
intro.cn: 本词是拉丁名词，由表方向的前缀、表「弯」的动词与名词后缀构成；同样的三部分也出现在英语同族词中，因此可以按部分读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- supplies direction, clinare supplies the bend, and the noun suffix names the state; the English word adds no further affix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表方向的前缀提供方向，表「弯」的动词提供弯曲义，名词后缀命名状态；英语词本身不再加缀。

items.example: The verb describes a body leaving the upright.
items.exampleCN: 该动词描述物体离开直立状态。

items.example: The prefixed verb added a direction to the bend.
items.exampleCN: 加前缀后，弯曲有了方向。

items.example: The noun named the state of leaning.
items.exampleCN: 该名词命名倾斜这一状态。

items.meaning: a tendency, a tilt or its measure
items.example: The tower's inclination is four degrees.
The path inclines toward the river.
The board is inclined at a low angle.
items.exampleCN: 木板以很小的角度倾斜。
委员会显得容易被说动。

items.meaning: an instrument for measuring a slope
the measured tilt of a line or plane
items.example: The inclination angle was recorded hourly.

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词后缀而得同族动词，语义偏移为「使倾斜；斜坡」
由动词加表完成状态的过去分词后缀构成，语义偏移为「倾斜的；倾向于……的」
由动词加表「可被……的」后缀构成，语义偏移为「易被说动的」
由动词词干加表测量仪器的成分构成，语义偏移为「测斜仪」
由本词加表角度的名词构成，语义偏移为「倾角」

definition_zh: 倾斜；倾向于；使倾向于；斜坡
definition_en: to lean or slope away from the vertical, to tend toward an opinion or action, and, as a noun, a sloping surface
core_image: 一根原本笔直的电线杆被风推得微微歪向一边
scene: 山路边的电线杆被风推得歪了一点，麻绳从杆子斜着垂下去。He is inclined to agree, though he wants to see the numbers first.
sceneCN: 这里 incline 是「倾向于」（第 2 个义项：心思往某个方向偏），句意是他倾向于同意，不过想先看看数字。画面里有山路、微微歪斜的电线杆和斜垂的麻绳。

pos.zh: 动词：倾斜、使倾斜；（使）倾向于
名词：斜坡、斜面

senses.title: To lean or slope
senses.definition: to lean away from an upright position, or to make something slope
senses.definitionCN: 离开直立的位置而偏斜，或使某物形成斜坡
senses.example: The old gate inclines slightly towards the road.
senses.exampleCN: 那扇旧门微微朝路边歪着。
senses.why: This is the physical sense, and the Latin root simply means to lean.
senses.whyCN: 这是身体性的义项，拉丁词根本来就是「倚、倾」的意思。

senses.title: To tend towards something
senses.definition: to have a tendency or a mild wish to think or act in a certain way
senses.definitionCN: 有某种倾向，或轻微地想做某事、持某种看法
senses.example: I incline to the view that the plan is too costly.
senses.exampleCN: 我倾向于认为这个方案代价太高。
senses.why: The mind leans the way a body leans, so the same verb describes opinions and wishes.
senses.whyCN: 心也会像身体那样往一边靠，于是同一个动词也能说看法与意愿。

senses.title: A sloping surface
senses.definition: a slope, especially one on a road or a railway
senses.definitionCN: 斜坡，尤指道路或铁路上的一段坡面
senses.example: The truck struggled up the long incline.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车吃力地爬上那段长坡。
senses.why: The verb turned into a noun and now names the thing that leans.
senses.whyCN: 动词转成名词后，直接指那个倾斜的东西本身。

intro.en: Incline goes back to a Latin verb for leaning, and the leaning of the head, the body, and the mind all use the same image.
intro.cn: incline 出自拉丁语中表示「倚靠」的动词，头、身体与心思的倾斜都用同一个意象。

items.en: Clinare meant to bend or lean, and it also lies behind the word climate, the slanted zone of the earth.
items.cn: 拉丁语 clinare 意为「弯、倚」，词语 climate（地球倾斜的地带）也从它而来。

items.en: Inclinare added in and meant to lean towards or upon something.
items.cn: inclinare 加上 in，意为「朝某物倾靠过去」。

items.en: Inclinatio named a leaning, and it was already used for a leaning of the mind.
items.cn: 名词 inclinatio 指倾斜，当时已用来比喻心思的偏向。

items.en: Old French carried the verb as incliner, still used of bodies, roofs, and opinions.
items.cn: 古法语以 incliner 沿用这个动词，既说身体、屋顶，也说看法。

items.en: English took it as incline, and the noun sense of a slope appeared later along with railway language.
items.cn: 英语借入后写作 incline，名词「斜坡」义则随铁路用语稍后出现。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the clin family of leaning; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of tendency.
note.cn: 形近组收 clin「倾」这一族词；近义组收表示「倾向于」的动词。

entries.definition: To lean away and so to go down or refuse; the opposite direction of incline.
entries.definitionCN: 「下降、拒绝」，同一词根方向朝下，与 incline 相对。

entries.definition: To lean back in a chair or on a bed.
entries.definitionCN: 「向后靠」，如靠在椅背或床上。

entries.definition: The noun partner, meaning a tendency or a slope.
entries.definitionCN: 名词形式，指倾向或倾斜度。

entries.definition: To be likely to do or be something over time.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「往往、有……的趋势」，多指长期倾向。

entries.definition: To bend the body or a thing to one side.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「倚、靠」，指身体或物体偏向一侧。

entries.definition: To rise or fall at an angle, as ground does.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「倾斜」，多用于地面与地形。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the body's lean visible inside the mental senses of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子让「身体倾斜」的画面在词的心理义里保持可见。

normal.en: To be inclined to do something is to lean towards it without yet walking.
normal.cn: be inclined to do 某事后，就是朝它歪了歪身子，还没迈步。

normal.en: Incline and decline differ by one prefix: leaning in versus leaning away.
normal.cn: incline 与 decline 只差一个前缀：一个往里靠，一个往外倒。

normal.en: The noun an incline is simply the slope you walk up, from the same word.
normal.cn: 名词 an incline 就是你走上去的那段坡，还是同一个词。

normal.en: The root also gave climate, the slanted band of the earth where the sun falls.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出了 climate，即太阳斜照的那一段地球。

normal.en: Disinclined flips the wish: not leaning, not willing.
normal.cn: disinclined 把意愿翻了过来：不倾身，也就是不乐意。

abstract.en: Opinions arrive as small inclinations before they harden into beliefs.
abstract.cn: 看法最初只是轻微的倾斜，后来才硬成信念。

abstract.en: Railway engineers needed a word for a gentle slope, and they borrowed the leaning of the human body.
abstract.cn: 铁路工程师需要给缓坡找个词，于是借用了人身体的倾斜。

abstract.en: The word quietly denies certainty: to incline is not to decide.
abstract.cn: 这个词悄悄否认了确定：倾向于，并不等于已经决定。

examples.en: The path inclines sharply after the second bridge.
examples.cn: 过了第二座桥，小路陡然而上。

examples.en: I am inclined to trust her account of the evening.
examples.cn: 我倾向于相信她对那天晚上的说法。

examples.en: The cyclist stood up for the final incline.
examples.cn: 骑手在最后那段坡上站了起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: in 向 + cline 倾——身子朝某边倾，就是「倾向于」

root: 拉丁语 inclinare「倾靠」（in + clinare「弯、倚」），经古法语 incliner 于中世纪英语时期进入英语；身体性的倾斜先引申为心思的倾向，铁路用语又派生名词「斜坡」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: leaning physically, tending in mind or wish, and a slope you can walk up.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：身体上的倾斜，心思或意愿上的倾向，以及可以走上去的斜坡。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a telephone pole pushed a little off upright by the wind, with a rope hanging at the same angle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根被风吹得微微歪斜的电线杆，麻绳也按同一个角度垂着。

branches.en: THE BODY: the verb starts as a physical lean.
branches.cn: 身体线：这个动词起初就是身体的倾斜。

branches.en: THE MIND: opinions lean before they settle.
branches.cn: 心思线：看法在定下来之前，先倾斜一下。

branches.en: THE ROAD: the noun names the slope itself.
branches.cn: 道路线：名词直接指那段坡。

branches.en: THE PHRASE: be inclined to do leaves room for doubt.
branches.cn: 搭配线：be inclined to do 给怀疑留了余地。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: inclination covers both the wish and the angle.
branches.cn: 词族线：inclination 同时指意愿与倾斜度。

intro.en: The table gathers members of the clin family, where the root means to bend or lean.
intro.cn: 此表汇集 clin 一族词，其词根意为「弯、倚」。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is clinare, to bend, with prefixes fixing the direction of the lean.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语底子是 clinare「弯」，前缀决定倾斜的方向。

items.example: The board inclines towards the left.
She has an inclination for drawing.
They were disinclined to move house again.

items.meaning: to lean down, to fall off

items.example: Recline the seat for the long flight.
items.exampleCN: 长途飞行时把座位往后放。

items.meaning: the band of earth where the sun slants
items.example: The climate here is dry and warm.

items.meaning: rising sharply, the extreme of an incline
items.meaningCN: 形容词：陡的，是斜坡的极端
items.exampleCN: 那条陡路把大家都累坏了。

definition_zh: 包括；包含；计入
definition_en: to have someone or something as a part of a larger group or whole
core_image: 敞开栅栏门，把站在外面的一个人也放进来
scene: 点名时总有人被漏掉，也总有人被补上。The price includes breakfast and one free drink.
sceneCN: 这里 include 是「包含」（第 1 个义项：整体之中含有一部分）；句意是价格里含早餐和一杯免费饮料。

pos.zh: 动词：包括；包含；计入

derivatives.zh: 由 include 加 -sion 构成，义为「包含、接纳」
义为「包含在内的、包容的」
义为「包括在内的」，常用于 tax included
义为「包括……在内」，作介词使用

senses.title: To contain as a part
senses.titleCN: 包含：作为整体的一部分
senses.definition: to have something as one of the parts of a whole
senses.definitionCN: 把某物作为整体的一部分而含有
senses.example: The price includes breakfast and one free drink.
senses.exampleCN: 价格包含早餐和一杯免费饮料。
senses.why: The Latin base claudere means to shut, and in-claudere shuts something inside the whole.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 claudere 意为「关闭」，in-claudere 就是把某物关进整体之内。

senses.title: To allow someone to join
senses.titleCN: 把……算进来：允许某人加入
senses.definition: to let a person become part of a group, list or activity
senses.definitionCN: 让某人成为群体、名单或活动的一部分
senses.example: Please include me in the next round of talks.
senses.exampleCN: 请把我也算进下一轮谈话。
senses.why: The fence image turns social: to include is to open the gate for a person standing outside.
senses.whyCN: 栅栏的意象转向人际：include 就是替站在外面的人打开门。

senses.title: To list something for attention
senses.titleCN: 列在文中：把某事写进内容
senses.definition: to mention a thing as part of a written list or set of details
senses.definitionCN: 作为书面清单或细节的一部分而提及
senses.example: The report includes three charts on rainfall.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告包含三张降雨图表。
senses.why: Writing is a container too: what is included is what the page holds.
senses.whyCN: 书写也是一种容器：被包含的东西就是页面所盛放的东西。

senses.title: Charged in addition to something
senses.definition: used on bills to show that a charge is already added
senses.definitionCN: 用于账单，表示某项费用已经加进去
senses.example: Service is included in the bill.
senses.exampleCN: 服务费已包含在账单里。
senses.why: Commercial use narrows the word to money: the sum already shuts the item in.
senses.whyCN: 商业用法把词收窄到金钱：总额已经把这一项关了进去。

intro.en: Include comes from Latin includere, to shut in, built from in, in, and claudere, to close.
intro.cn: include 来自拉丁语 includere「关在里面」，由 in「在内」与 claudere「关闭」构成。

items.en: Claudere meant to shut a door, and in-claudere meant to shut something inside.
items.cn: claudere 意为「关门」，in-claudere 则是「把某物关在里面」。

items.en: Classical writers used includere for enclosing a place or a list of names.
items.cn: 古典作家用 includere 表示围住一块地方或把名字列入其中。

items.en: Church and legal texts used it for items counted within a document.
items.cn: 教会与法律文本用它表示计入某文件之内的条目。

items.en: English took include for parts held inside a whole.
items.cn: 英语借 include 表示被整体所容纳的部分。

items.en: The social sense of admitting people grew in the last two centuries.
items.cn: 「接纳人」的社会义项在近两百年里发展起来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -clude shape; the near-meaning group holds verbs of holding something as part of a whole.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -clude 外形；近义组收表示「作为一部分含有」的动词。

entries.definition: To keep someone or something out on purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「排除、不让进入」，与 include 反义同根。

entries.definition: To finish or to reach a judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「结束、得出结论」，与 include 同根。

entries.definition: The act of making someone part of a group.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「包含、接纳」。

entries.definition: To hold something inside.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「装有、包含」，更偏物理容纳。

entries.definition: To deal with or pay for something as well.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「涵盖、支付」，多用于范围与费用。

entries.definition: To make something a necessary part of an activity.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「涉及、需要含有」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the closed-door image, the ex-contrast and the everyday price tag.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借关门意象、ex- 对照与日常价签。

normal.en: In plus clude is in plus shut: include shuts the item inside the whole.
normal.cn: in 加 clude 就是「在内」加「关闭」：include 把条目关进整体里。

normal.en: Exclude has the same root with ex-, which means out, so the pair is gate open and gate shut.
normal.cn: exclude 同根但用 ex-「向外」，这一对就是开门与关门。

normal.en: Inclusive marks the price tag: what is included is already in the sum.
normal.cn: inclusive 写在价签上：被包含的已经算在总额里。

normal.en: Include me in is the social version of opening the fence.
normal.cn: include me in 就是「打开栅栏」的社交版本。

normal.en: A good report includes the awkward chart too, not only the handsome one.
normal.cn: 好的报告连那张不好看的图表也包含进去，而不只挑好看的。

abstract.en: To include is to decide that a boundary is wide enough for one more thing.
abstract.cn: 包含就是判定一道边界足够宽，还能再装下一件东西。

abstract.en: What a language includes shapes what its speakers can easily think.
abstract.cn: 一门语言包含什么，就塑造了说这门语言的人容易想到什么。

abstract.en: Whole and part only make sense together: include is the hinge between them.
abstract.cn: 整体与部分只有放在一起才有意义：include 就是两者的铰链。

examples.en: The tour includes two nights in a small hotel.
examples.cn: 这趟旅行包含在一家小旅馆住两晚。

examples.en: Her duties include answering the phone.
examples.cn: 她的职责包括接电话。

examples.en: Please include your student number on the form.
examples.cn: 请在表格上写上你的学号。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印库路得」——把货物印进库房，就算包含入库里了。

root: 拉丁语 in（在内）+ claudere（关闭）→ includere（关在里面）；同根词有 exclude、conclude、preclude、inclusion、inclusive。

sensesIntro.en: Include shuts a thing inside a whole, and from that single image come containing parts, admitting people, listing details and charging sums.
sensesIntro.cn: include 把某物关进整体之中，仅凭这一意象就生出了含部分、接纳人、列细节与计费四路含义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fence gate opened long enough for one more person to step in.
core.cn: 核心意象：栅栏门敞开一会儿，让又一个人走进来。

branches.en: PART LINE: the whole holds the part inside.
branches.cn: 部分线：整体把部分容纳在内。

branches.en: PEOPLE LINE: someone outside is brought into the group.
branches.cn: 人的线：外面的人被带进群体里。

branches.en: PAGE LINE: a document holds the detail in print.
branches.cn: 页面线：文件用文字把细节收进去。

branches.en: MONEY LINE: the bill already shuts the charge in.
branches.cn: 金钱线：账单已经把这一项关了进去。

branches.en: ETHICS LINE: boundaries decide who is counted and who is not.
branches.cn: 伦理线：边界决定谁被算在内、谁不算。

intro.en: A Latin prefix for inside, a root for closing, and a family of words about boundaries.
intro.cn: 一个表「在内」的拉丁前缀、一个表「关闭」的词根，加一族与边界有关的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin in, in, and claudere, to shut, gave includere, to shut in.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in「在内」与 claudere「关闭」合成 includere「关在里面」。

items.example: the root of exclude and include
items.exampleCN: exclude 与 include 的共同词根

items.meaning: the state of being shut in
items.example: the inclusion of a new member

items.exampleCN: 第十页到第二十页含首尾

definition_zh: 包含的；包括在内的；包容的（不排斥任何群体）；（范围）含端点的
definition_en: including a particular person, group or limit rather than leaving it out
core_image: 一圈人围坐，桌子原本留着一个缺口，后来缺口处也摆上一把椅子，圈就此闭合
scene: 礼堂的座位原本只排到侧门，工作人员又搬来几把椅子，把最后一排补满。An inclusive admissions policy welcomes applicants from every region and every income level.
sceneCN: 这里指「不排斥任何群体、把所有人都纳入」（第 1 个义项：范围上包含所有人）；句意为不排斥的招生政策欢迎来自每个地区和每个收入水平的申请者。可辨识物件：礼堂座椅、侧门、登记桌、名单、台阶。

pos.zh: 包容的；不排斥任何群体的
包括在内的；含（某物）的
（范围）含端点的；全部费用在内的

senses.title: Leaving no group out
