senses.definition: including everyone in a group, service or institution, especially people who are often excluded
senses.definitionCN: 把一个群体、服务或机构向所有人开放，尤其是常被排除在外的人
senses.example: An inclusive admissions policy welcomes applicants from every region and every income level.
senses.exampleCN: 不排斥的招生政策欢迎来自每个地区和每个收入水平的申请者。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to shut in'; an inclusive rule shuts the gate only after everyone has been brought inside.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词本义是「关在里面」；一条包容的规则是在所有人都被带进来之后才关门。

senses.title: Including the stated item
senses.titleCN: 把所提到的事物包括在内
senses.definition: covering a named item as part of a total, often in the phrase inclusive of
senses.definitionCN: 把提到的事物计入总数，常用于「包括……在内」这一说法
senses.example: The quoted price is inclusive of delivery and insurance.
senses.exampleCN: 所报价格包含运费与保险。
senses.why: The word marks the boundary of a total: what lies inside the line is counted, what lies outside is not.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标出总数的边界：线内之物计入，线外之物不计。

senses.title: One price covering everything
senses.titleCN: 一价全包、费用全部计入
senses.definition: describing a price or package that covers all costs, so no extra charge follows
senses.definitionCN: 描述涵盖全部费用的价格或套餐，事后不再另收费
senses.example: They booked an all-inclusive stay where meals and transfers were covered.
senses.exampleCN: 他们订了一次一价全包的行程，餐食与接送都包含在内。
senses.why: The boundary sense turned commercial: the total is closed, and nothing is left outside it to be billed later.
senses.whyCN: 边界义进入商业语境：总数被封闭起来，外面不再留下任何可另行收费的项目。

senses.title: Counting both endpoints
senses.definition: counting the first and last values as part of a stated range
senses.definitionCN: 把所给范围的首尾数值都计入其中
senses.example: Read pages ten to twenty inclusive before the seminar.
senses.exampleCN: 研讨课之前读完第十页到第二十页，含首尾两页。
senses.why: A closed interval is drawn with solid ends; the word says the ends are inside the line, not outside it.
senses.whyCN: 闭区间用实心端点画出；这个词表示端点在线内，而不在线外。

senses.title: Language that names everyone
senses.titleCN: 照顾到所有人的语言表达
senses.definition: using words that do not assume one gender, culture or group and leave others invisible
senses.definitionCN: 使用不预设某一种性别、文化或群体、也不让其他人隐形的措辞
senses.example: The style guide recommends inclusive language that names both parents.
senses.exampleCN: 体例指南建议使用同时提到双亲的包容性措辞。
senses.why: A phrase can have a margin too: whichever group is not named is left outside the sentence.
senses.whyCN: 措辞也有边缘：没有被提到的那群人就留在句子之外。

senses.title: Classrooms built for all pupils
senses.titleCN: 让所有学生都能参与的课堂
senses.definition: describing schooling in which pupils with different needs learn together with shared support
senses.definitionCN: 描述不同需求的学生在共同支持下一起学习的教育安排
senses.example: The district moved toward inclusive classrooms with shared support staff.
senses.exampleCN: 该学区转向融合课堂，并配备共享的支持人员。
senses.why: The social sense settled into education, where the test of inclusion is whether a pupil sits inside the ordinary room.
senses.whyCN: 社会义进入教育领域，衡量的标准就是学生是否被安置在普通教室里。

senses.title: Growth that reaches the edge
senses.definition: describing economic growth that raises incomes and opportunities for low-income groups as well as the average
senses.definitionCN: 描述不仅提高平均值、也提高低收入群体收入与机会的经济增长
senses.example: Economists now ask whether growth is inclusive, not merely fast.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家现在追问增长是否包容，而不只看它是否快速。
senses.why: If growth stays in the centre, the margin receives nothing; an inclusive economy carries the gain to the edge.
senses.whyCN: 增长若只留在中心，边缘什么也得不到；包容的经济把收益带到边缘。

senses.title: A pronoun that includes the listener
senses.titleCN: 语言学中把听者包括在内的代词
senses.definition: describing a first person plural form that includes the person addressed as well as the speaker
senses.definitionCN: 描述既包括说话者、也包括受话者的第一人称复数形式
senses.example: In some languages an inclusive first person plural includes the listener.
senses.exampleCN: 有些语言的第一人称复数包含式把听者也包括在内。
senses.why: Grammar drew the same line: an inclusive form keeps the listener inside the circle, an exclusive form leaves the listener outside.
senses.whyCN: 语法沿用了同一条界线：包含式把听者留在圈内，排除式把听者留在圈外。

intro.en: Inclusive comes from Medieval Latin inclusivus, from Latin includere 'to shut in', built on in- 'in' and claudere 'to shut, close'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: inclusive 来自中世纪拉丁 inclusivus，再往上出自拉丁 includere「关在里面」，由 in-「在内」与 claudere「关闭」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Claudere meant 'to shut, close, enclose'. Its deeper origin is not established; the link sometimes suggested to clavis 'key' is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: claudere 意为「关闭、围住」。其更深来源未得到证明；有人把它与 clavis「钥匙」联系起来，那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: In- 'in' plus claudere produced includere 'to shut in, enclose, include'.
items.cn: in-「在内」加 claudere 构成 includere「关在里面、围住、包括」。

items.en: Medieval Latin formed inclusivus to describe something that encloses or counts another item within it.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁构成 inclusivus，用来描述把另一项围在或计入自身之内的事物。

items.en: English adopted the adjective in the fifteenth century, first in the sense of enclosing or comprising.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪引入这个形容词，最初表示「围住」或「包含」。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word was applied to schools, workplaces and growth, where the question is who is left outside the gate.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个词被用于学校、职场与经济增长，问题变成谁被留在门之外。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Latin source of claudere is unsettled, and no exact first citation is recorded for the social sense, so dates here are approximations.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：claudere 在拉丁语之前的来源无定论，社会义也没有确切的最早书证，因此这里给出的年代均为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same shutting-in root in other parts of speech; group two holds adjectives of wide or welcoming scope.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「关在里面」词根、词性不同的词；第二组是表示范围宽广或态度欢迎的形容词。

entries.definition: To bring something inside a group or total; inclusive is the adjective describing such a total.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物带入一个群体或总数；inclusive 是描述这种总数的形容词。

entries.definition: Means 'having been counted in'; it marks an item already inside, while inclusive marks the boundary that lets it in.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「已被计入的」；它标记已在内部的项目，而 inclusive 标记放它进来的那条边界。

entries.definition: The act or state of being brought inside; the adjective describes the quality, the noun names the thing itself.
entries.definitionCN: 被带入内部的动作或状态；形容词描述性质，名词指事物本身。

entries.definition: Means in a way that leaves nothing out; it modifies how a list or rule is applied.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「以不遗漏任何一项的方式」；修饰清单或规则被适用的方式。

entries.definition: Covering all or nearly all parts of a subject; it stresses completeness of content, not openness to people.
entries.definitionCN: 涵盖一个主题的全部或几乎全部；强调内容的完整，而非对人的开放。

entries.definition: Describing a place or person that makes outsiders feel wanted; it names the emotional effect of inclusion.
entries.definitionCN: 描述让外来者感到被接纳的场所或人；它指包容带来的情感效果。

entries.definition: Covering a wide range; it can describe a category without saying who is treated fairly inside it.
entries.definitionCN: 涵盖范围广；可描述一个类别，却不说明其中谁被公平对待。

entries.definition: Applying to every member without exception; stronger than inclusive because it allows no local variation.
entries.definitionCN: 无例外地适用于每一成员；比 inclusive 更强，因为它不留地方性差异。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real shutting-in root, the real derivatives and the real policy phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「关在里面」词根、真实的派生词与真实的政策搭配。

normal.en: The Latin verb meant 'to shut in', so an inclusive rule closes the door only after everyone is inside.
normal.cn: 拉丁动词意为「关在里面」，因此包容的规则是在所有人都进来之后才关门。

normal.en: The family runs include, included, inclusion, inclusive, inclusively, inclusiveness and inclusivity.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 include、included、inclusion、inclusive、inclusively、inclusiveness 与 inclusivity。

normal.en: Policy phrases mark the modern sense: inclusive education, inclusive growth, inclusive language, all-inclusive.
normal.cn: 政策搭配标出现代义：融合教育、包容性增长、包容性语言、一价全包。

normal.en: The boundary sense survives in the arithmetic phrase 'ten to twenty inclusive'.
normal.cn: 边界义保留在算术说法「第十到第二十，含首尾」中。

normal.en: The prefix in- also appears in include and inclusion, all from the same Latin verb.
normal.cn: 前缀 in- 同样出现在 include 与 inclusion 中，都出自同一个拉丁动词。

abstract.en: Picture a circle of chairs with one gap, and a late guest filling that gap so the circle closes.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈椅子留着一个缺口，一位迟到的客人坐进缺口，圆圈就此闭合。

abstract.en: Picture a gate that stays open until the last person has walked through, then shuts behind everyone.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门一直开着，直到最后一个人走过，才在所有人身后关上。

abstract.en: Picture a receipt with no line left for extras, because every cost was written inside the total.
abstract.cn: 想象一张账单，没有任何一行留给额外费用，因为每项成本都已写进总数。

examples.en: The library runs an inclusive reading hour for children of every ability.
examples.cn: 图书馆为各种能力的孩子开设包容性阅读时段。

examples.en: The fare is inclusive of taxes, so the final bill will not change.
examples.cn: 票价已含税，因此最终账单不会再变。

examples.en: Count the seats from the first row to the fifth inclusive.
examples.cn: 座位从第一排数到第五排，含首尾两排。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「里面」加「关」——先把所有人都关进圈内，再合上门 → 包容的、包括在内的

root: inclusive 来自中世纪拉丁 inclusivus，再往上出自拉丁 includere「关在里面」= in-「在内」+ claudere「关闭」。claudere 在拉丁语之前的更深来源不确定；与 clavis「钥匙」的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line: a boundary is drawn so that nothing and nobody is left outside. The line is applied to a group, a price, a range, a wording, a classroom, an economy and finally to the grammar of who counts as 'we'.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条线展开：画一条边界，使任何人与任何事物都不被留在外面。这条线依次用于群体、价格、范围、措辞、课堂、经济，最后用于「我们」是否包括听者的语法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circle of chairs with its last gap filled.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈椅子，最后一个缺口也被补上。

branches.en: THE CLOSED CIRCLE: the first sense fills the last empty chair so that no group stays outside.
branches.cn: 闭合的圆圈：第一个义项补上最后一把空椅，使任何群体都不留在外面。

branches.en: THE LINE ITSELF: a total or a range counts what lies inside, including both ends.
branches.cn: 线本身：总数或范围只计入线内之物，两端也包括在内。

branches.en: THE SEALED PRICE: every cost is written inside the total, leaving nothing to bill later.
branches.cn: 封住的价格：每项成本都写进总数，事后不再收费。

branches.en: ROOM IN THE SENTENCE AND THE CLASS: wording and schooling must also leave a chair for everyone.
branches.cn: 句子与教室里的位置：措辞与教育同样必须给每个人留一把椅子。

branches.en: GAIN AND GRAMMAR: prosperity reaches the margin, and the pronoun keeps the listener inside the circle.
branches.cn: 收益与语法：繁荣抵达边缘，代词把听者留在圈内。

intro.en: The word can be read from a Latin prefix meaning 'in', a Latin verb for shutting, a medieval adjective ending and the derived words built on the same stem.
intro.cn: 这个单词可以按表示「在内」的拉丁前缀、表示关闭的拉丁动词、中世纪形容词后缀以及同一词干上的派生词逐段读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- and claudere together give include and the whole family; the adjective ending -ive marks a quality, and -ity turns it into a noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 in- 与 claudere 合成 include 与整个词族；形容词后缀标记性质，名词后缀再把它变成名词。

items.example: The prefix places the action inside a boundary.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作放进一条边界之内。

items.structure: claudere, clausi, clausum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The Latin verb supplies the closing image.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词提供「关闭」的意象。

items.meaning: to shut in; to count as part of a group
the act or state of being included
items.example: The inclusion of new voices changed the report.
items.exampleCN: 新声音的加入改变了这份报告。

items.meaning: tending to include; leaving nothing out
items.meaningCN: 倾向于包含的；不遗漏的
items.example: The policy is inclusive of part-time workers.
items.exampleCN: 这项政策把兼职工作者也包括在内。

items.example: The list was read inclusively, from the first name to the last.
items.exampleCN: 名单从第一个名字读到最后，首尾都算在内。

items.example: Reviewers praised the inclusiveness of the design.
items.exampleCN: 评审者称赞这项设计的包容性。

items.meaningCN: 有意识地接纳所有群体的做法
items.example: The agency published targets for inclusivity.
items.exampleCN: 该机构公布了包容性目标。

items.example: Breakfast is included in the room rate.
The ending turns a verb into a describing word.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成描述性词语。

derivatives.meaning: to take in as part of a whole
the act or state of being included
in a way that leaves nothing out
the quality of being open to all

definition_zh: 收入；收益；所得
definition_en: the money a person or business receives regularly from work or investments
core_image: 工资单上的数字顺着账本一栏流进来，落在月底的余额上
scene: 月底算账时，最先要看的是进账与支出。Her monthly income barely covers the rent.
sceneCN: 这里 income 是「收入」（第 1 个义项：定期得到的钱）；句意是她每月的收入勉强够付房租。

pos.zh: 名词：收入；收益；所得

derivatives.zh: 由 out 与 come 构成，义为「结果」，与 income 结构相对
义为「支出、开销」，与 income 相反
义为「工资、劳动所得」，是 income 的一种具体来源

senses.title: Money received from work
senses.definition: the money that comes in regularly from a job or business
senses.definitionCN: 由工作或经营定期进来的钱
senses.example: Her monthly income barely covers the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 她每月的收入勉强够付房租。
senses.why: The word is literally what comes in, so its first home is the household budget.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面上就是「进来的东西」，所以它的第一个归宿是家庭账本。

senses.title: Money from investments
senses.definition: profit that arrives from savings, rent or shares rather than from labour
senses.definitionCN: 来自储蓄、房租或股票的收益，而非劳动所得
senses.example: Rent from the second flat is his only extra income.
senses.exampleCN: 第二套房子的租金是他唯一的额外收益。
senses.why: Any stream that flows in counts, whether it is paid by an employer or by an asset.
senses.whyCN: 凡是流进来的钱都算，无论付款方是雇主还是资产。

senses.title: A group's or country's revenue
senses.titleCN: 总收入：集体或国家的岁入
senses.definition: the total money that a company or a country takes in over a period
senses.definitionCN: 公司或国家在一段时间内的总进账
senses.example: Tourism provides a large share of the island's income.
senses.exampleCN: 旅游业提供了这座岛收入的一大部分。
senses.why: The same metaphor scales up: households, firms and nations all keep a ledger.
senses.whyCN: 同一个比喻可以放大：家庭、公司和国家的账本都是同样的记法。

senses.title: In economics, a flow of money
senses.titleCN: 所得：经济学中的流量概念
senses.definition: in economics, the flow of money received by a person or sector in a period
senses.definitionCN: 经济学中，个人或部门在一段时期内收到的货币流量
senses.example: Economists compare income with consumption rather than with wealth.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家把所得与消费比较，而不是与财富比较。
senses.why: The discipline needs a noun for a flow, and this compound supplies exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科需要一个指「流量」的名词，而这个合成词恰好提供。

intro.en: Income is a native English compound of in and come, first meaning simply what comes in.
intro.cn: income 是英语本土合成词，由 in 与 come 组成，最初只表示「进来的东西」。

items.en: Inncome and incuman described the act of coming in.
items.cn: inncome 与 incuman 描述「进来」这一动作。

items.en: The noun shifted from the act to the thing that arrives.
items.cn: 名词从「进来的动作」转指「到来的东西」。

items.en: By the seventeenth century income was used for revenue from land or trade.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，income 已用于指土地或贸易带来的收入。

items.en: Income tax made the word an everyday term in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪的所得税让这个词成为日常用语。

items.en: Economics gave it a technical sense as a flow measured per period.
items.cn: 经济学又给了它「按时期计量流量」的专业含义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -come frame; the near-meaning group holds words for money received.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -come 框架；近义组收表示「收到的钱」的词。

entries.definition: The result that comes out of a process.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「结果」，与 income 结构相同。

entries.definition: A greeting given to a guest who comes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「欢迎」，含 come 一词。

entries.definition: Arriving or about to arrive.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「进来的、即将到来的」。

entries.definition: A fixed payment made monthly or yearly.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「薪水」，指固定发放的报酬。

entries.definition: Money paid for work by the hour or day.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「工资」，多按小时或按天计。

entries.definition: Money a business or government takes in.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「营收、岁入」，更正式。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the literal come-in reading, the balanced ledger and the tax form.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借字面的「进来」含义、收支账本与税表。

normal.en: Income is simply what comes in, a two-word sentence packed into one noun.
normal.cn: income 就是「进来的东西」，把一个两词句压进一个名词。

normal.en: Outcome is the mirror: what comes out of a process is a result, not money.
normal.cn: outcome 是镜像：从过程里「出来」的是结果，不是钱。

normal.en: Income tax takes a slice of what has just come in.
normal.cn: income tax 是从刚进来的钱里切走一片。

normal.en: A steady income is a steady stream, which is why the money verbs are flow and run out.
normal.cn: steady income 是稳定的水流，所以谈钱会说 flow 或 run out。

normal.en: On a payslip the word sits at the top, above every deduction.
normal.cn: 在工资单上，这个词印在最上面，压在所有扣款之上。

abstract.en: Income measures a door that keeps opening, not a box that is already full.
abstract.cn: 收入衡量的是不断打开的门，而不是已经装满的箱子。

abstract.en: A budget is a story about which direction one prefers to face, inward or outward.
abstract.cn: 预算是一个关于你愿意朝哪边看的故事：向内还是向外。

abstract.en: To live on an income is to let a river decide the width of every bank.
abstract.cn: 靠一份收入生活，就是让一条河决定两岸的宽度。

examples.en: His income doubled after he changed jobs.
examples.cn: 换工作之后他的收入翻了一倍。

examples.en: The family lives on a fixed income.
examples.cn: 这家人靠固定收入生活。

examples.en: Low income often decides which school a child attends.
examples.cn: 低收入常常决定一个孩子上哪所学校。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「银卡姆」——银卡里的钱慢慢进来，就是收入。

root: 古英语 in「在内、进入」+ come「来」，字面义为「进来的东西」；对照 outcome、incoming。

sensesIntro.en: Income starts as a literal coming in, then widens from wages to investment returns, to a nation's revenue and to a technical flow.
sensesIntro.cn: income 起初只是字面的「进来」，后来从工资扩展到投资收益、国家岁入，再到专业上的流量概念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a column of figures flowing in and settling at the month-end balance.
core.cn: 核心意象：一栏数字流进来，落在月底的余额上。

branches.en: WORK LINE: a job sends money in every month.
branches.cn: 工作线：每月由工作送来钱。

branches.en: ASSET LINE: rent and shares send money in without labour.
branches.cn: 资产线：房租与股票不需劳动就能送钱进来。

branches.en: SCALE LINE: firms and countries keep the same ledger.
branches.cn: 规模线：公司与国家用的是同一本账。

branches.en: THEORY LINE: economics measures the flow per period.
branches.cn: 理论线：经济学按时期计量这股流量。

branches.en: LEDGER LINE: income is always read against spending.
branches.cn: 账本线：收入永远要对着支出一起看。

intro.en: A Germanic preposition of coming in, joined with a Germanic verb, and a small family of -come words.
intro.cn: 一个表「进来」的日耳曼介词与一个日耳曼动词组合，形成一族以 -come 结尾的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin equivalents are in and venire, which gave English words like revenue and invent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的对应成分是 in 与 venire，英语由此得到 revenue、invent 等词。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 归还，由此得到「收益」之义

definition_zh: 包含；吸收；合并
definition_en: to take something into a larger whole so that it becomes one part of it
core_image: 两块面团被揉在一起，再也分不清哪块是新的
scene: 改稿时常常把别人的建议揉进自己的段落里。The new plan incorporates ideas from every department.
sceneCN: 这里 incorporate 是「吸收合并」（第 2 个义项：把某物并进更大的整体）；句意是新计划吸收了各部门的想法。

pos.zh: 动词：包含；吸收；合并
形容词：合并的；一体化的（多用于法律文本）

derivatives.zh: 由 incorporate 加 -ion 构成，义为「合并、法人化」
义为「已合并的、组成法人的」，公司名后常缩写为 Inc.
义为「公司的、团体的」，与本词同根

senses.title: To contain as an integrated part
senses.titleCN: 包含：作为整体中的一部分
senses.definition: to include something so that it forms part of a whole
senses.definitionCN: 把某物纳入其中，使其成为整体的一部分
senses.example: The device incorporates a camera and a speaker.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设备里集成了摄像头和扬声器。
senses.why: The Latin corpus, body, supplies the image: something is given a body inside a larger body.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 corpus「身体」提供了意象：某物被放进更大的身体里，获得了一个位置。

senses.title: To absorb ideas or material
senses.titleCN: 吸收：把想法或材料并进来
senses.definition: to take in suggestions, methods or substances and make them one's own
senses.definitionCN: 把建议、方法或材料吸收进来变成自己的
senses.example: The new plan incorporates ideas from every department.
senses.exampleCN: 新计划吸收了各部门的想法。
senses.why: Dough is the natural picture: once kneaded, the added piece cannot be taken back out.
senses.whyCN: 面团是最自然的画面：一旦揉进去，加进来的那块就取不出来了。

senses.title: To combine into one body
senses.titleCN: 合并：把两个单位并成一个
senses.definition: to unite two organizations or territories into a single unit
senses.definitionCN: 把两个组织或地区并成一个单位
senses.example: The two villages were incorporated into one town.
senses.exampleCN: 两个村庄合并成了一个镇。
senses.why: Law extends the body image to groups: several bodies may become one body.
senses.whyCN: 法律把身体意象扩展到团体：几个身体合成一个身体。

senses.title: To form a legal company
senses.definition: to establish a business as a legal corporation
senses.definitionCN: 把一家企业设立为法律上的法人公司
senses.example: They incorporated the business last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 他们去年春天把这家企业注册成了公司。
senses.why: A company receives a legal body of its own, which is exactly what the root promises.
senses.whyCN: 公司获得了自己的法律身体，这正是词根所许诺的意思。

intro.en: Incorporate comes from Late Latin incorporare, to give a body to, from in and corpus, body.
intro.cn: incorporate 来自晚期拉丁语 incorporare「赋予身体」，由 in 与 corpus「身体」构成。

items.en: Corpus meant a body, and also a body of writing or of people.
items.cn: corpus 意为「身体」，也指一批文字或一群人。

items.en: Incorporare meant to unite things into one body.
items.cn: incorporare 意为把多个事物联合成一个身体。

items.en: English used incorporate for mixing substances and ideas into a whole.
items.cn: 英语用 incorporate 表示把材料与想法混入整体。

items.en: Legal use produced the sense of forming a corporation.
items.cn: 法律用法产生了「组成法人公司」的含义。

items.en: Modern business writing uses it for features built into a product.
items.cn: 现代商务写作又用它表示产品里内置的功能。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the corpor- body root; the near-meaning group holds verbs of joining things into one.
note.cn: 形近组共用表示「身体」的 corpor- 词根；近义组收表示「合为一体」的动词。

entries.definition: Relating to a large company.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「公司的、团体的」。

entries.definition: A company treated as one legal person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「公司、法人团体」。

entries.definition: The act of uniting into one body.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「合并、法人化」。

entries.definition: To combine parts into a working whole.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「整合」，强调配合成完整系统。

entries.definition: To join two things so that they become one.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「合并」，多用于机构。

entries.definition: To take something in and make it part of oneself.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「吸收」，强调吞入并同化。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the body root, the kneaded dough and the company register.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借「身体」词根、揉面的动作与公司注册。

normal.en: In plus corporate: put a body inside a body, and the smaller one loses its outline.
normal.cn: in 加 corporate：把一个身体放进另一个身体，小的那个就失去了轮廓。

normal.en: Corpus is body, so corporation is a group given one legal body.
normal.cn: corpus 是身体，所以 corporation 就是被赋予一个法律身体的团体。

normal.en: Kneading dough is the best demonstration: after folding, no one can find the seam.
normal.cn: 揉面团是最好的演示：折过之后没人找得到接缝。

normal.en: Inc. after a company name is this word cut short.
normal.cn: 公司名后的 Inc. 就是这个词的缩写。

normal.en: A good editor incorporates the reader's question without letting it show.
normal.cn: 好编辑会把读者的疑问吸收进去，却不让人看出来。

abstract.en: To incorporate is to make difference disappear without erasing its contribution.
abstract.cn: 吸收就是让差异消失，却不清除它带来的贡献。

abstract.en: Every culture grows by incorporating what it first called foreign.
abstract.cn: 每种文化都靠吸收当初称为「外来」的东西而成长。

abstract.en: A whole is strong when it can still name the parts it has taken in.
abstract.cn: 一个整体之所以强，是因为它仍叫得出自己吸收过哪些部分。

examples.en: The recipe incorporates a little honey for sweetness.
examples.cn: 这个食谱加了一点蜂蜜来增甜。

examples.en: Teachers incorporate games into the first lesson.
examples.cn: 老师们把游戏融入第一堂课。

examples.en: The firm was incorporated in nineteen ninety.
examples.cn: 这家公司于一九九零年注册成立。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因科破瑞」——因为把学科破开重揉，就合并成了一门新学问。

root: 拉丁语 in（进入）+ corpus（身体）→ incorporare（赋予身体、合为一体）；同根词有 corporate、corporation、corpse、corps。

sensesIntro.en: Incorporate gives an incoming thing a body inside a larger body, so the word covers containing features, absorbing ideas, merging units and creating legal persons.
sensesIntro.cn: incorporate 让进来的东西在更大的身体里获得位置，因此涵盖内置功能、吸收想法、合并单位与成立法人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two lumps of dough folded until the seam cannot be found.
core.cn: 核心意象：两块面团折叠到找不出接缝。

branches.en: PRODUCT LINE: a feature is built into the whole.
branches.cn: 产品线：某项功能被造进整体里。

branches.en: IDEA LINE: advice is kneaded into a plan.
branches.cn: 想法线：建议被揉进计划里。

branches.en: UNION LINE: two units are given one body.
branches.cn: 联合线：两个单位拥有同一个身体。

branches.en: LAW LINE: a business receives a legal body.
branches.cn: 法律线：企业获得法律意义上的身体。

branches.en: CRAFT LINE: the maker hides the joins but keeps the strength.
branches.cn: 手艺线：制作者把接缝藏起来，却保留强度。

intro.en: A Latin prefix for inside, a root meaning body, and a verb ending for making.
intro.cn: 一个表「在内」的拉丁前缀、一个意为「身体」的词根，以及表示「使之成为」的动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin corpus, body, with in and -are, gave incorporare, to make into one body.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 corpus「身体」结合 in 与 -are，构成 incorporare「使成一体」。

items.example: a body and a corpse share one root
items.exampleCN: 身体与尸体同出一个词根

definition_zh: 增加；增长；增大
definition_en: to become larger in amount, number or degree, or to make something larger
core_image: 温度计里的红线一节一节往上爬
scene: 入冬后，早高峰的公交总是一年比一年挤。Ticket prices increase every January.
sceneCN: 这里 increase 是「上涨」（第 1 个义项：数量或程度变大）；句意是票价每年一月上涨。

pos.zh: 动词：增加；增长；增大
名词：增加；增长；增量

derivatives.zh: 义为「不断增加的」，如 increasing pressure
义为「减少」，与 increase 反义同构

senses.title: To grow in amount or number
senses.definition: to become larger in size, amount or number
senses.definitionCN: 在规模、数量或数目上变大
senses.example: Ticket prices increase every January.
senses.exampleCN: 票价每年一月上涨。
senses.why: The Latin crescere means to grow, and in-crescere is to grow into something bigger.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 crescere 意为「生长」，in-crescere 就是长成更大的样子。

senses.title: To make something larger
senses.definition: to raise a figure, level or output by one's own action
senses.definitionCN: 通过自身行动把数字、水平或产量提高
senses.example: The factory plans to increase output by a fifth.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂计划把产量提高五分之一。
senses.why: The verb is both intransitive and transitive, because growth can happen or be caused.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词既可不及物也可及物，因为增长既可以自己发生，也可以被促成。

senses.title: To become stronger in degree
senses.definition: to become greater in intensity, such as pain, pressure or risk
senses.definitionCN: 在强度上变大，如疼痛、压力或风险
senses.example: Noise from the road increases at night.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里路上的噪音会增大。
senses.why: Not everything that grows is countable: pressure and pain also swell.
senses.whyCN: 并非所有增长都能计数：压力与疼痛也会膨胀。

senses.title: The noun, a rise in amount
senses.definition: a rise in amount, price or level, often measured against an earlier figure
senses.definitionCN: 数量、价格或水平的上升，常与先前数字相较
senses.example: There was a sharp increase in rainfall last summer.
senses.exampleCN: 去年夏天降雨量急剧增加。
senses.why: English turns the verb into a noun without changing its shape, only its stress.
senses.whyCN: 英语把这个动词直接变成名词，形状不变，只挪动重音。

senses.title: In phrases, on the rise
senses.titleCN: 在增加中：用于固定短语
senses.definition: used in the phrase on the increase to mean becoming more common
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 on the increase，表示日益增多
senses.example: Cheating in exams is on the increase.
senses.exampleCN: 考试作弊的现象在增多。
senses.why: The noun settles into a fixed idiom that reports a trend rather than a single event.
senses.whyCN: 名词固定成一个习语，用来报道趋势而不是单次事件。

intro.en: Increase comes from Latin increscere, to grow in, from in and crescere, to grow.
intro.cn: increase 来自拉丁语 increscere「在里面生长」，由 in 与 crescere「生长」构成。

items.en: Crescere meant to grow, as plants and children do.
items.cn: crescere 意为「生长」，如植物与孩子长大。

items.en: French encreistre carried the word into everyday use about crops and wealth.
items.cn: 法语 encreistre 把这个词带入关于收成与财富的日常用法。

items.en: English borrowed it as encresen, first as a verb only.
items.cn: 英语借作 encresen，最初只有动词用法。

items.en: The noun appeared in the fourteenth century with a different stress pattern.
items.cn: 名词在十四世纪出现，并带有不同的重音模式。

items.en: Statistics and economics made both forms central to reporting trends.
items.cn: 统计学与经济学让两种形式都成为报道趋势的核心词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -crease growth root; the near-meaning group holds verbs of going up.
note.cn: 形近组共用表示「生长」的 -crease 词根；近义组收表示「上升」的动词。

entries.definition: To become smaller in amount.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「减少」，与 increase 反义同根。

entries.definition: More and more over time.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「日益、越来越」。

entries.definition: A small regular addition.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「增量、增额」。

entries.definition: To go up, often used of prices and levels.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「上升、上涨」。

entries.definition: To become larger over time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「生长、增长」，更偏自然过程。

entries.definition: To become larger in size or scope.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「扩大」，偏规模与体积。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the growing root, the thermometer and the stress shift between verb and noun.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借「生长」词根、温度计和动名之间的重音移动。

normal.en: In plus crease: growth happens inside the thing itself, not bolted on from outside.
normal.cn: in 加 crease：生长发生在事物内部，不是从外面钉上去的。

normal.en: Decrease is the same root with de-, so the pair is a rising and a falling line.
normal.cn: decrease 同根但用 de-，这一对就是上升线与下降线。

normal.en: Stress moves: inCREASE as a verb, INcrease as a noun, a common English habit.
normal.cn: 重音会挪：动词读 inCREASE，名词读 INcrease，这是英语常见习惯。

normal.en: On the increase means the trend line is still climbing.
normal.cn: on the increase 意思是趋势线还在往上爬。

normal.en: Increase by is the size of the jump, while increase to is where it lands.
normal.cn: increase by 指跳了多少，increase to 指跳到哪里。

abstract.en: Growth is the only change that keeps its own shape as it changes.
abstract.cn: 增长是唯一在变化中仍保持自身形状的变化。

abstract.en: A number that increases never explains itself; the reason always sits outside the chart.
abstract.cn: 一个增加的数字从不解释自己，原因永远在图表之外。

abstract.en: What increases without limit is usually the thing nobody is measuring.
abstract.cn: 无限增长的，往往正是没人去计量的那样东西。

examples.en: The number of students increased by nearly a hundred.
examples.cn: 学生人数增加了将近一百。

examples.en: Exercise can increase your energy level.
examples.cn: 锻炼能提高你的精力水平。

examples.en: The company reported an increase in sales.
examples.cn: 公司报告销售额有所增长。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因快死」——人数因疫情快速变化，增长的忧愁里带着个快字。

root: 拉丁语 in（在内）+ crescere（生长）→ increscere（长起来）；同根词有 decrease、increment、crescent、concrete。

sensesIntro.en: Increase says that something grows inside its own frame, and the word then extends from counts to intensity and finally to a noun for a trend.
sensesIntro.cn: increase 说的是某物在自己的框架里长起来，于是从数量扩展到强度，最后成为表示趋势的名词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the red line in a thermometer climbing notch by notch.
core.cn: 核心意象：温度计里的红线一格一格往上爬。

branches.en: COUNT LINE: numbers of things get larger.
branches.cn: 数量线：事物的数目变大。

branches.en: ACTION LINE: someone raises output on purpose.
branches.cn: 行动线：有人有意提高产量。

branches.en: DEGREE LINE: pressure and noise swell.
branches.cn: 程度线：压力与噪音一起膨胀。

branches.en: NOUN LINE: the rise itself becomes a thing to report.
branches.cn: 名词线：上升本身变成一个可报道的对象。

branches.en: IDIOM LINE: a fixed phrase describes a trend.
branches.cn: 习语线：固定说法描述一种趋势。

intro.en: A Latin prefix for inward growth and a root for growing, plus a large family of -crease words.
intro.cn: 一个表「向内生长」的拉丁前缀与表示「生长」的词根，加上一族 -crease 词。

latinIntro.en: Latin crescere, to grow, gave increscere, to grow on, and English took both halves.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 crescere「生长」生出 increscere「长起来」，英语把两部分都借了过来。

items.example: the root of increase and decrease
items.exampleCN: increase 与 decrease 的共同词根

definition_zh: 难以置信的；惊人的；极好的
definition_en: too strange or extreme to be believed, or extremely good
core_image: 听见一句话，眉毛先跳起来，嘴还没张开
scene: 朋友说自己一夜游过海峡，你第一反应是不信。It sounds incredible, but she finished the race in under three hours.
sceneCN: 这里 incredible 是「难以置信的」（第 1 个义项：难以相信）；句意是听起来难以置信，但她不到三小时就跑完了全程。

pos.zh: 形容词：难以置信的；惊人的；极好的

derivatives.zh: 义为「难以置信地；极其」，由本词加 -ly 构成
义为「可信的」，去掉 in- 即成肯定形式
义为「信任、信用」，与本词同根

senses.title: Too strange to believe
senses.titleCN: 难以置信：奇怪到无法相信
senses.definition: so unusual or extreme that it is hard to believe
senses.definitionCN: 极其反常或极端，令人难信
senses.example: It sounds incredible, but she finished the race in under three hours.
senses.exampleCN: 听起来难以置信，但她不到三小时就跑完了全程。
senses.why: The Latin credere means to believe, and the negative prefix in- says no: not to be believed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 credere 意为「相信」，否定前缀 in- 说「不」：不可被相信。

senses.title: Extremely large or great
senses.titleCN: 惊人的：规模或程度极大
senses.definition: so great in size or amount that it surprises the mind
senses.definitionCN: 在规模或数量上大到让人吃惊
senses.example: The team worked at incredible speed.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团队以惊人的速度工作。
senses.why: When a number passes belief, the same word measures size rather than truth.
senses.whyCN: 当一个数字超出相信的范围，同一个词就转而衡量大小而非真伪。

senses.title: Extremely good, in speech
senses.definition: used informally to praise something as wonderful
senses.definitionCN: 口语中用来称赞某物好极了
senses.example: The view from the top was incredible.
senses.exampleCN: 山顶的景色美极了。
senses.why: Praise borrows the same exclamation: what is beyond belief is also beyond the ordinary.
senses.whyCN: 赞叹借用了同一句惊叹：超出相信的，也超出寻常。

senses.title: Hard to accept, used of behaviour
senses.titleCN: 难以接受：形容行为过分
senses.definition: used of behaviour that seems shockingly unfair or careless
senses.definitionCN: 形容行为不公或粗心到令人震惊
senses.example: It is incredible that they left the door unlocked.
senses.exampleCN: 他们竟没锁门，真让人难以接受。
senses.why: The negative prefix carries moral weight too: such conduct should not be believed of anyone.
senses.whyCN: 否定前缀也带道德分量：这种行为不该被相信会出自任何人。

intro.en: Incredible comes from Latin incredibilis, from in-, not, and credere, to believe.
intro.cn: incredible 来自拉丁语 incredibilis，由 in-（不）与 credere（相信）构成。

items.en: Credere meant to trust or to entrust, the source of credit and creed.
items.cn: credere 意为「信任、托付」，是 credit 与 creed 的来源。

items.en: Incredibilis named what could not be believed, often of marvels.
items.cn: incredibilis 指令人无法相信之事，常用于奇闻。

items.en: English borrowed it through French for tales that defied belief.
items.cn: 英语经由法语借入，用于不合常理的故事。

items.en: The sense widened from untrue to merely astonishing.
items.cn: 词义从「不真」扩展到「仅仅令人吃惊」。

items.en: Spoken English added the sense of extremely good.
items.cn: 英语口语又添上「极好」的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cred- believe root; the near-meaning group holds words of surprise.
note.cn: 形近组共用表示「相信」的 cred- 词根；近义组收表示「惊异」的词。

entries.definition: Able to be believed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可信的」，与本词只差一个 in-。

entries.definition: In a way that is hard to believe.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「难以置信地」。

entries.definition: Trust that allows buying now and paying later.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「信用、赊账」，同根。

entries.definition: Impossible or very hard to believe.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「难以置信的」，更口语。

entries.definition: So surprising that one is stunned.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「惊人的」，重在看后发懵。

entries.definition: Very surprising and impressive.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人惊叹的」，偏褒义。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the believe root, the cred-credible pair and the everyday exclamation.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借「相信」词根、cred/credible 对照与日常惊叹。

normal.en: Credit and creed both hold cred, believe, so incredible means simply not-credible.
normal.cn: credit 与 creed 里都含 cred「相信」，所以 incredible 就是「不可信的」。

normal.en: Take away in- and credible remains, which makes the pair the easiest negative in English.
normal.cn: 去掉 in- 剩下 credible，这一对是英语里最好记的否定搭配。

normal.en: When a story is incredible, the eyebrow moves before the mouth does.
normal.cn: 故事令人难以置信时，眉毛先于嘴巴做出反应。

normal.en: The same word praises dinner and prices, because both can pass belief.
normal.cn: 同一个词既夸晚饭也形容价格，因为两者都可能超出想象。

normal.en: An incredible amount is not a claim about truth but about the size of the pile.
normal.cn: an incredible amount 不是在说真假，而是在说那一堆有多大。

abstract.en: Belief is the most portable currency: it buys claims, goods and people alike.
abstract.cn: 相信是最通用的货币：它能买到说法、货物与人。

abstract.en: What is incredible is not always false, only unwitnessed.
abstract.cn: 难以置信的不一定假，只是尚未被亲眼看见。

abstract.en: Every wonder starts as a sentence the listener refuses to accept.
abstract.cn: 每一件奇事起初都是一句听者拒绝接受的话。

examples.en: They made an incredible amount of noise.
examples.cn: 他们弄出了惊人的动静。

examples.en: Her recovery was incredible to the doctors.
examples.cn: 她的康复让医生们难以置信。

examples.en: What an incredible meal that was!
examples.cn: 那顿饭真是好极了！

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因克瑞德」——因一张信用卡被克扣，账单令人难以置信。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ credere（相信）→ incredibilis；同根词有 credible、credit、credibility、creed、credential。

sensesIntro.en: Incredible begins as the simple denial of belief, then measures size, and finally becomes a spoken word of praise.
sensesIntro.cn: incredible 起初只是对「相信」的简单否定，后来用来衡量大小，最后变成口语中的赞美。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: eyebrows jumping before the mouth can answer.
core.cn: 核心意象：嘴巴还没开口，眉毛先跳了起来。

branches.en: TRUTH LINE: the tale resists belief.
branches.cn: 真伪线：故事抗拒被相信。

branches.en: SIZE LINE: a quantity passes the limit of imagination.
branches.cn: 大小线：数量越过想象的边界。

branches.en: PRAISE LINE: everyday speech turns it into a compliment.
branches.cn: 赞美线：日常口语把它变成褒义词。

branches.en: JUDGEMENT LINE: conduct is judged too unlikely to accept.
branches.cn: 评判线：某种行为被判为难以接受。

branches.en: TONE LINE: one adjective can be a doubt or a compliment.
branches.cn: 语气线：同一个形容词既可是疑问也可是称赞。

intro.en: A negative prefix on a root meaning believe, with an adjective ending that makes it describable.
intro.cn: 一个否定前缀加意为「相信」的词根，再接形容词词尾，使之可用来形容事物。

latinIntro.en: Latin in-, not, plus credere, to believe, plus -ibilis, able to be, gave incredibilis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in-「不」加 credere「相信」加 -ibilis「可……的」，构成 incredibilis。

items.exampleCN: credible 与 credit 的词根

definition_zh: 反复灌输；谆谆教诲；使养成
definition_en: to fix an idea or habit in someone's mind by constant repetition
core_image: 一个人一次又一次把同一句话写在同一块湿泥上，直到字迹再也抹不掉
scene: 祖父每晚讲同一个故事，讲到最后孩子自己会背了。Years of inculcating caution had made her careful without thinking.
sceneCN: 这里 inculcate 指反复灌输（第 1 个义项：靠重复把观念植入心中）；句意为多年灌输谨慎，让她不假思索就小心。

pos.zh: 反复灌输；谆谆教诲；使养成

senses.title: Teach by repetition
senses.definition: to make an idea stick by saying or showing it again and again
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复说或反复示范使一个观念扎下根
senses.example: Years of inculcating caution had made her careful without thinking.
senses.exampleCN: 多年灌输谨慎，让她不假思索就小心。
senses.why: The word assumes that repetition does the work that argument cannot.
senses.whyCN: 这个词假定，重复能做成论证做不到的事。

senses.title: Instil values
senses.definition: to plant moral beliefs so deep that they guide behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 把道德信念植得足够深以指导行为
senses.example: The school set out to inculcate honesty rather than merely to punish lying.
senses.exampleCN: 学校要灌输诚实，而不只是惩罚说谎。
senses.why: A value that is only known is weak; one that is inculcated acts before it is examined.
senses.whyCN: 只是被知道的价值观很弱；被灌输的那一个在受检验之前就已行动。

senses.title: Implant a habit
senses.definition: to train a behaviour until it needs no conscious decision
senses.definitionCN: 把一个行为训练到不需要有意识决定
senses.example: She inculcated the habit of checking the locks twice.
senses.exampleCN: 她养成了检查两遍门锁的习惯。
senses.why: A habit is a decision that has been handed over to the body.
senses.whyCN: 习惯是被交给身体去执行的决定。

senses.title: Drill a rule
senses.definition: to teach a rule through repeated practice and correction
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复练习与纠正来教一条规则
senses.example: The coach inculcated one rule at a time and would not move on early.
senses.exampleCN: 教练一次只灌输一条规则，不肯提前推进。
senses.why: Drilling works because the body remembers what the mind forgets.
senses.whyCN: 训练之所以有效，是因为身体记得心智所忘的。

senses.title: Inculcate obedience
senses.definition: to train a person to comply without questioning
senses.definitionCN: 把一个人训练到不加质疑地顺从
senses.example: The regime inculcated obedience through daily ritual.
senses.exampleCN: 该政权通过每日仪式灌输服从。
senses.why: Here the word turns critical: repetition can install compliance as easily as virtue.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词转为批评：重复既能装进美德，也能装进顺从。

senses.title: Inculcate caution
senses.definition: to make someone habitually careful about risk
senses.definitionCN: 使某人习惯性地对风险保持小心
senses.example: His parents inculcated caution with stories of near misses.
senses.exampleCN: 他的父母用险些出事的经历灌输谨慎。
senses.why: Caution taught through story arrives with feeling attached, which is why it lasts.
senses.whyCN: 借故事教来的谨慎带着情感，因此能留下来。

senses.title: Inculcate through example
senses.definition: to transmit a belief by consistently acting it out
senses.definitionCN: 通过一贯地做出某种行为来传递信念
senses.example: She inculcated fairness less by speech than by how she divided the work.
senses.exampleCN: 她灌输公平，与其说靠言语，不如说靠如何分派工作。
senses.why: Example is the strongest form of repetition, because it shows the belief in use.
senses.whyCN: 榜样是最强的重复形式，因为它展示了信念在使用中的样子。

senses.title: Inculcation resisted
senses.definition: the process by which a taught belief is finally refused
senses.definitionCN: 被教导的信念最终被拒绝的过程
senses.example: The students endured years of inculcation and then rejected most of it.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们忍受了多年灌输，然后拒绝了其中大部分。
senses.why: What is implanted can also be dug out, though the roots usually remain.
senses.whyCN: 被植入的东西也能被挖出来，尽管根通常还在。

intro.en: Inculcate comes from Latin for trampling in, the picture of a heel pressing an idea into soft ground.
intro.cn: inculcate 来自拉丁语「踩进去」，画面是脚跟把一个观念压进松软的地面。

items.en: Inculcare meant 'to trample in, to force upon', built from in- and calcare.
items.cn: inculcare 意为「踩进去、强加」，由 in- 与 calcare 构成。

items.en: Calcare 'to tread' comes from calx, the heel, and gives the sense of pressure from above.
items.cn: calcare「踩踏」出自 calx（脚跟），带来自上而下的压力感。

items.en: Calx meant heel; Roman soldiers and farmers both knew the weight of one.
items.cn: calx 意为脚跟；罗马士兵与农夫都懂得一只脚跟的重量。

items.en: English took the verb in the 16c., at first for teaching by forceful repetition.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个动词，最初指靠强力重复来教。

items.en: Modern English keeps the tone: the word is neutral in education and critical in politics.
items.cn: 现代英语保留这种语气：在教育中中性，在政治中带批评。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the tread root; the near-meaning group names ways of implanting ideas.
note.cn: 形近组共享「踩」的词根；近义组列出植入观念的不同方式。

entries.definition: tending to implant by repetition.

entries.definition: to keep eggs warm until they hatch.

entries.definition: to put a feeling or idea in gradually.
entries.definitionCN: 逐渐放入情感或观念。

entries.definition: to fix an idea firmly in the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 把观念牢牢固定于心中。

entries.definition: to teach beliefs that must not be questioned.
entries.definitionCN: 教授不许质疑的信条。

entries.definition: to train by repeated exercise.
entries.definitionCN: 通过重复练习训练。

normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「脚跟把字压进湿泥、直到抹不掉」的画面。

normal.en: Inculcate contains calx, the heel: the idea is stepped into the mind.
normal.cn: inculcate 含 calx（脚跟）：观念是被踩进心里的。

normal.en: Think of a path worn into grass by the same pair of shoes.
normal.cn: 想象同双鞋在草地上踩出一条路。

normal.en: Say in-KUL-kate; the middle sounds like a firm press downward.
normal.cn: 读成 in-KUL-kate，中间音像一次坚定的下压。

normal.en: Link with calc, heel: pressure from above is the whole image.
normal.cn: 和 calc（脚跟）联系：自上而下的压力就是整个画面。

normal.en: Pair it with repetition: inculcation is repetition with a destination.

abstract.en: Repetition can build a virtue or a cage, and it does not ask which.
abstract.cn: 重复既能造美德，也能造笼子，而它不问是哪一种。

abstract.en: What is pressed in deeply is hard to remove, even after it is rejected.
abstract.cn: 被压得很深的东西很难移除，即使被拒绝之后。

abstract.en: Example teaches faster than instruction because it shows the idea working.
abstract.cn: 榜样比训导教得快，因为它展示观念在运作。

definition_zh: 补偿；赔偿；赔偿保证；免责保障
definition_en: a promise to compensate someone for a loss or to protect them from liability, or the money paid under such a promise
core_image: 一个人把对方手里的账单接过来，替他把钱付清
scene: 仓库失火后，保险勘察员站在焦黑的货架间核对清单。The policy gave the owner an indemnity for the burned stock.
sceneCN: 这里 indemnity 是「保险赔偿」（第 3 个义项：保险人就承保损失作出的补偿）；句意：保单为被烧毁的存货给业主提供了一笔赔偿。

pos.zh: 名词：补偿；赔偿；赔偿保证；免责保障

derivatives.zh: 由本词加动词后缀构成，义为「赔偿；使免受损失或责任」
由 indemnify 加名词后缀构成，义为「赔偿；免责保障」
由 indemnify 加过去分词后缀构成，义为「已获赔偿的；受保障的」

senses.title: The promise to cover a loss
senses.definition: a promise by one party to compensate another for a specified loss or damage
senses.definitionCN: 一方承诺就特定损失或损害向另一方作出补偿
senses.example: The parent company gave an indemnity to cover the debts of the subsidiary.
senses.exampleCN: 母公司提供了赔偿保证，以承担子公司的债务。
senses.why: Latin in- means not and damnum means loss, so indemnity begins as the state of being without loss.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 in- 表示「不」，damnum 表示「损失」，所以 indemnity 起初指「不受损失」的状态。

senses.title: The money paid under a promise
senses.definition: the sum paid to make good a loss under such a promise
senses.definitionCN: 依据这类承诺为填补损失而支付的款项
senses.example: The builder received an indemnity for the delay in delivery.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑商就交货延迟获得了一笔补偿金。
senses.why: The promise becomes concrete as money: what was lost is weighed and paid back in cash.
senses.whyCN: 承诺落实为金钱：损失被折算成数额，再用现金补回去。

senses.title: Insurance compensation
senses.definition: payment by an insurer to restore the insured to the financial position held before the loss
senses.definitionCN: 保险人支付的款项，使被保险人回到损失发生前的经济状况
senses.example: The insurer settled the claim with an indemnity equal to the market value.
senses.exampleCN: 保险人以相当于市场价值的赔偿结清了索赔。
senses.why: Insurance is the purest form of the idea: a pool of money keeps the insured person free from the loss.
senses.whyCN: 保险是这一观念最纯粹的形式：一笔共同资金让被保险人免受损失。

senses.title: Protection against liability
senses.definition: a contractual promise to protect another party from legal liability or the cost of claims
senses.definitionCN: 合同中的承诺，保护另一方免受法律责任或索赔成本
senses.example: The contractor accepted a broad indemnity in favour of the client.
senses.exampleCN: 承包商接受了有利于客户的一项宽泛免责保障。
senses.why: Loss can also be a legal burden; keeping a party free from loss means keeping the claim off that party.
senses.whyCN: 损失也可以是法律负担；让一方不受损失，就是把索赔挡在它之外。

senses.title: An indemnity clause
senses.definition: a term in a contract that sets out who must cover losses and claims arising from the deal
senses.definitionCN: 合同中的条款，规定由谁承担交易引起的损失与索赔
senses.example: The indemnity in clause eight survives the end of the agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 第八条中的赔偿条款在协议结束后仍然有效。
senses.why: A promise needs a place in the text, so the clause is the promise written down and given a boundary.
senses.whyCN: 承诺需要在文本中有个位置，条款就是写下来并被划定了边界的承诺。

senses.title: A letter or deed of indemnity
senses.definition: a document in which a person or bank promises to cover a loss, often used to release goods without the usual papers
senses.definitionCN: 个人或银行承诺承担损失的书面文件，常用于在缺少常规单据时放行货物
senses.example: The bank issued a letter of indemnity so the cargo could be released.
senses.exampleCN: 银行出具了赔偿保证书，使货物得以放行。
senses.why: When the usual papers are missing, the document itself carries the promise and lets the goods move.
senses.whyCN: 常规单据缺失时，这份文件本身承载承诺，让货物得以流转。

senses.title: Exemption from penalty
senses.definition: a grant of freedom from a penalty or from prosecution, especially by law
senses.definitionCN: 免于处罚或免于起诉的授予，尤指由法律规定
senses.example: An act of indemnity protected the officials from prosecution.
senses.exampleCN: 一项赦免法使那些官员免于起诉。
senses.why: The old legal sense extends the image from loss of money to loss of freedom: indemnity removes the threatened penalty.
senses.whyCN: 古老的法律义把意象从金钱损失扩展到自由损失：indemnity 撤除了悬在头上的处罚。

senses.title: A war indemnity
senses.definition: money that a defeated state is required to pay to the victor to cover the costs and losses of war
senses.definitionCN: 战败国被要求向战胜国支付的、用于弥补战争成本与损失的款项
senses.example: The treaty fixed the war indemnity at three billion francs.
senses.exampleCN: 条约把战争赔款定为三十亿法郎。
senses.why: Between states the loss is measured in whole economies, and the payment that covers it is still called an indemnity.
senses.whyCN: 国家之间的损失以整个经济来计量，而弥补这笔损失的付款仍然叫 indemnity。

intro.en: Indemnity is Latin in- plus damnum, loss: the word starts as freedom from loss and grows into the promise that keeps someone free from it.
intro.cn: indemnity 是拉丁语 in- 加 damnum（损失）：这个词从「不受损失」起步，发展为让人免受损失的那项承诺。

items.en: Damnum means loss or harm, and it is the base of the whole family.
items.cn: damnum 意为损失或损害，是整个词族的基础。

items.en: In- negates damnum: indemnis means unharmed, free from loss.
items.cn: in- 否定 damnum：indemnis 意为未受损害的、不受损失的。

items.en: Indemnitas names security against loss and, in law, exemption from penalty.
items.cn: indemnitas 指免受损失的保障，在法律中也指免于处罚。

items.en: The noun passes into French as indemnite, keeping both the security and the exemption senses.
items.cn: 这个名词以 indemnite 的形式进入法语，同时保留保障与免罚两种含义。

items.en: Indemnity is recorded in English in the fifteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: indemnity 于十五世纪见于英语；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Insurance and commercial contracts turn indemnity into a standard promise to cover another party.
items.cn: 保险与商业合同把 indemnity 变成替另一方承担损失的标准承诺。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the English family built on indemnify; the near-meaning group gathers other ways of covering a loss.
note.cn: 形近组收围绕 indemnify 构成的英语词族；近义组收其他弥补损失的方式。

entries.definition: To compensate someone for a loss or to protect them from liability.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「赔偿、使免受损失或责任」，是本词的动词形式。

entries.definition: The act of compensating a loss or protecting a party from claims.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「赔偿行为、免责保障」，由 indemnify 加名词后缀构成。

entries.definition: Compensated for a loss, or protected against a claim.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「已获赔偿的、受保障的」，是 indemnify 的过去分词形式。

entries.definition: Money paid to make up for a loss, an injury, or work done.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「补偿、赔偿金」，是一般用语，不必然含合同承诺。

entries.definition: A contract in which a company covers a specified loss in return for regular payments.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「保险」，指以定期付费换取承保损失的合同。

entries.definition: A promise that something will be done or that a product will work, often backed by a repair or refund.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「保证、担保」，承诺某事一定做到或商品一定可用，常以维修或退款作后盾。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin parts in- and damnum, the English family, and the legal phrases the noun appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语成分 in- 与 damnum、英语词族，以及这个词实际出现的法律搭配。

normal.en: in- means not and damnum means loss, so indemnity is the promise that keeps a loss away.
normal.cn: in- 是「不」，damnum 是「损失」，所以 indemnity 是让损失不落到你身上的承诺。

normal.en: The verb is indemnify, the act is indemnification, and the protected party is indemnified.
normal.cn: 动词是 indemnify，行为是 indemnification，受保障的一方是 indemnified。

normal.en: An indemnity clause decides who pays when a third party brings a claim.
normal.cn: indemnity clause 决定第三方提出索赔时由谁付钱。

normal.en: A letter of indemnity lets goods move when the usual papers are missing.
normal.cn: letter of indemnity 让货物在缺少常规单据时仍可放行。

normal.en: In history, an act of indemnity wipes out a threatened penalty rather than a bill.
normal.cn: 在历史上，act of indemnity 抹掉的是悬着的处罚，而不是一张账单。

abstract.en: See a hand taking a bill out of another hand and paying it at the counter.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从另一只手里接过账单，替他在柜台付清。

abstract.en: See a cheque covering the exact cost of a burned shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象一张支票正好覆盖被烧毁货架的成本。

abstract.en: See a wide umbrella held over a warehouse while the rain pours down.
abstract.cn: 想象大雨倾盆时，一把大伞撑在仓库上方。

examples.en: The contract contains an indemnity clause covering third-party claims.
examples.cn: 合同中有一条涵盖第三方索赔的赔偿条款。

examples.en: The insurer paid an indemnity for the flooded warehouse.
examples.cn: 保险人为被淹的仓库支付了一笔赔偿。

examples.en: The defeated country was forced to pay a heavy war indemnity.
examples.cn: 战败国被迫支付巨额战争赔款。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因登米提」——把损失挡在门外，账单由别人接过去付清；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不、无）+ damnum（损失）→ indemnis（未受损失的）→ indemnitas（免受损失、免罚）→ 古法语 indemnité → 英语 indemnity；核心义「使人不受损失」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of indemnity apply one promise, to keep a person free from loss: a contract promise, a payment, insurance, protection from liability, a clause, a document, exemption from penalty, and a war payment.
sensesIntro.cn: indemnity 的八个义项都围绕同一项承诺——让人免受损失：合同承诺、实际付款、保险、责任保障、条款、文书、免罚与战争赔款。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person takes the bill from another hand and pays it at the counter.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人从对方手里接过账单，替他在柜台付清。

branches.en: THE PROMISE: a spoken promise and a written letter both carry the same undertaking.
branches.cn: 承诺线：口头承诺与书面保证书承载的是同一项承担。

branches.en: THE MONEY: the promise is cashed as a payment, and insurance is its most organised form.
branches.cn: 金钱线：承诺兑现为付款，保险则是它最有组织的形式。

branches.en: THE LIABILITY LINE: contract terms shift claims away from the protected party.
branches.cn: 责任线：合同条款把索赔从受保障一方身上移开。

branches.en: THE PENALTY: the old legal sense removes punishment rather than paying a bill.
branches.cn: 处罚线：古老的法律义撤除的是处罚，而不是支付账单。

branches.en: THE STATE: a defeated country pays for war losses on the same pattern.
branches.cn: 国家线：战败国按同样的模式为战争损失付钱。

intro.en: Indemnity is Latin in- plus damnum, and English adds indemnify, indemnification and the adjective indemnified around it.
intro.cn: indemnity 是拉丁语 in- 加 damnum，英语围绕它扩展出 indemnify、indemnification 与形容词 indemnified。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- means not, and damnum means loss; indemnis is unharmed, and indemnitas is security against loss.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in- 意为「不」，damnum 意为「损失」；indemnis 是未受损害的，indemnitas 是免受损失的保障。

items.example: The prefix turns loss into freedom from loss.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「损失」变成「不受损失」。

items.example: Damnum supplies the loss at the centre of the word.
items.exampleCN: damnum 提供这个词中央的「损失」。

items.meaningCN: 未受损害的；不受损失的
items.example: Indemnis is the adjective made of the prefix and the noun.
items.exampleCN: indemnis 是由前缀与名词构成的形容词。

items.example: Indemnitas is the direct Latin source of indemnity.
items.exampleCN: indemnitas 是 indemnity 的直接拉丁语来源。
后缀 -itas 构成抽象名词。

items.meaning: a promise to cover a loss
items.example: Indemnity keeps the Latin noun sense.
items.exampleCN: indemnity 保留拉丁语名词的含义。

items.meaning: to compensate for loss, protect from liability
items.example: Indemnify is the verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: indemnify 是这一词族的动词。

items.example: Indemnification names the act rather than the promise.
items.exampleCN: indemnification 指的是行为，而不是承诺本身。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 未受损害的；不受损失的

definition_zh: 独立；自主；不受支配
definition_en: freedom from control by another person, group or country
core_image: 一只鸟第一次不再靠着巢沿，自己张开翅膀
scene: 搬出父母家，才真正懂得独立是什么味道。Living alone taught her independence.
sceneCN: 这里 independence 是「独立」（第 1 个义项：不依赖他人）；句意是独自生活教会了她独立。

pos.zh: 名词：独立；自主；不受支配

derivatives.zh: 义为「独立的」，是本词的形容词形式
义为「依赖」，去掉 in- 即成相反名词

senses.title: Freedom from another's control
senses.definition: the state of not being controlled or supported by another person
senses.definitionCN: 不被他人控制或供养的状态
senses.example: Living alone taught her independence.
senses.exampleCN: 独自生活教会了她独立。
senses.why: The word is in- not plus depend, to hang from, so independence means not hanging from anyone.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 in-（不）加 depend（悬靠），所以独立就是不再挂在任何人身上。

senses.title: A nation's self-rule
senses.definition: the freedom of a country to govern itself
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家自行治理的自由
senses.example: The country declared independence in nineteen sixty.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家在一九六零年宣布独立。
senses.why: Politics simply lifts the personal image to the scale of a whole people.
senses.whyCN: 政治只是把个人的意象放大到整个民族的尺度。

senses.title: Money that needs no patron
senses.titleCN: 经济独立：不靠他人供养
senses.definition: having enough income to live without help from others
senses.definitionCN: 拥有足够收入、无需他人帮助也能生活
senses.example: A part-time job gave him financial independence.
senses.exampleCN: 一份兼职让他经济上独立了。
senses.why: Money is the modern rope that ties people to each other, so cutting it makes them independent.
senses.whyCN: 金钱是现代社会把人系在一起的绳索，剪断它人便独立了。

senses.title: Separateness in thought or method
senses.titleCN: 独立性：思想或方法上自成一体
senses.definition: the quality of forming one's own judgement rather than copying others
senses.definitionCN: 形成自己的判断而非照搬他人的品质
senses.example: Her research shows real independence of mind.
senses.exampleCN: 她的研究显示出真正的思想独立性。
senses.why: Beyond bodies and borders, the word describes a mind that does not lean on another.
senses.whyCN: 除了身体与国界，这个词还形容一颗不倚靠别人的心。

intro.en: Independence is in-, not, plus dependence, from Latin dependere, to hang from.
intro.cn: independence 是 in-（不）加 dependence，后者源自拉丁语 dependere「悬挂于」。

items.en: Dependere meant to hang down from something, from de- and pendere.
items.cn: dependere 意为「从某物上垂挂」，由 de- 与 pendere 构成。

items.en: Depend entered English with the sense of being supported by another.
items.cn: depend 进入英语时带有「依靠他人支撑」之义。

items.en: Independence appeared in the seventeenth century for freedom from control.
items.cn: independence 在十七世纪出现，表示不受控制。

items.en: Political use spread after the American Declaration in seventeen seventy-six.
items.cn: 一七七六年美国《独立宣言》之后，政治用法广泛流传。

items.en: Personal and financial senses grew in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 个人与经济层面的义项在十九、二十世纪发展起来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the pend- hang root; the near-meaning group holds words of freedom and self-rule.
note.cn: 形近组共用表示「悬挂」的 pend- 词根；近义组收表示自由与自决的词。

entries.definition: Free from control by others.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「独立的」。

entries.definition: The state of needing help.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「依赖」。

entries.definition: A person who depends on another by custom or law.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「受抚养者」。

entries.definition: The power to act as one wishes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「自由」。

entries.definition: The right of a group to govern itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「自治」，多为术语。

entries.definition: Reliance on one's own powers.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「自力更生」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the hanging root, the bird leaving the nest and the declaration of independence.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借「悬挂」词根、离巢的鸟与独立宣言。

normal.en: Depend is to hang down from someone, so independence is the moment the hook is removed.
normal.cn: depend 是挂在某人身上，那么独立就是钩子被取下的时刻。

normal.en: The verb is depend, the adjective independent, the noun independence: only the ending changes.
normal.cn: 动词 depend、形容词 independent、名词 independence，只换词尾。

normal.en: Dependence and independence face each other with one small in- between.
normal.cn: dependence 与 independence 只隔一个小小的 in-。

normal.en: A baby bird at the nest edge is the best picture: first it flaps, then it lets go.
normal.cn: 巢沿的雏鸟是最好的画面：先扇翅，再放手。

normal.en: Independence Day celebrates a document that ended a hanging rope across the ocean.
normal.cn: 独立日纪念的是一纸文书，它剪断了横跨大洋的那根绳。

abstract.en: Independence is measured not by who you leave but by who no longer has to carry you.
abstract.cn: 独立不看离开了谁，而看谁不必再把你背着。

abstract.en: True autonomy keeps the link but gives it a looser knot.
abstract.cn: 真正的自主保留联结，只把绳结放松。

abstract.en: A mind that never leans will never know what it believes.
abstract.cn: 从不倚靠的心，也不会知道自己相信什么。

examples.en: She values her independence more than a big salary.
examples.cn: 比起高薪，她更看重自己的独立。

examples.en: The colony fought for independence.
examples.cn: 这块殖民地曾为独立而战。

examples.en: Learning to cook is a first step towards independence.
examples.cn: 学会做饭是迈向独立的第一步。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印地盆等次」——自己占地印盆，不必等别人赏赐，便是独立。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ dependere（悬挂于，来自 de- + pendere「悬挂」）→ independence；同根词有 depend、dependent、pendant、suspend。

sensesIntro.en: Independence begins as the removal of an outer hook, then scales to a country's self-rule, to money without a patron, and to a mind that judges for itself.
sensesIntro.cn: independence 起初是不再挂在钩上，而后扩展到国家的自主、无须供养人的财富，以及自做判断的心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a young bird letting go of the nest edge on its first flight.
core.cn: 核心意象：雏鸟第一次放手离巢。

branches.en: PERSONAL LINE: no one else gives the orders.
branches.cn: 个人线：不再由他人发号令。

branches.en: POLITICAL LINE: a country governs itself.
branches.cn: 政治线：国家自行治理。

branches.en: MONEY LINE: income arrives without a patron.
branches.cn: 金钱线：收入不必来自恩主。

branches.en: MIND LINE: judgement is formed alone.
branches.cn: 思想线：判断由自己形成。

branches.en: GROWTH LINE: independence is usually won step by step.
branches.cn: 成长线：独立往往一步一步赢来。

intro.en: A negative prefix, a prefix meaning down, a root meaning hang and a noun ending.
intro.cn: 一个否定前缀、一个表示「向下」的前缀、一个意为「悬挂」的词根，以及一个名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin pendere, to hang, with de-, down, gave dependere, to hang from; in- then denies it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pendere「悬挂」加 de-「向下」成为 dependere「悬于」，再加 in- 加以否定。

items.example: the root of suspend and pendant
items.exampleCN: suspend 与 pendant 的词根

items.meaning: to hang from, to rely on
state of not hanging from others
to hang up, to stop for a time

definition_zh: 独立的；自主的；不相关的
definition_en: not controlled by or relying on other people or things
core_image: 两根柱子之间没有横梁相连，各自立着
scene: 两个人可以意见不同，却依旧是朋友。She is independent enough to make her own decision.
sceneCN: 这里 independent 是「独立的」（第 1 个义项：自主做决定）；句意是她足够独立，能自己做决定。

pos.zh: 形容词：独立的；自主的；不相关的
名词：无党派人士（少见）

derivatives.zh: 义为「独立地」，由本词加 -ly 构成
义为「依赖的」，去掉 in- 即成相反形式

senses.title: Able to act or decide alone
senses.titleCN: 独立的：能自主行动或决定
senses.definition: able to do things or make decisions without help from others
senses.definitionCN: 能够不需他人帮助做事或做决定
senses.example: She is independent enough to make her own decision.
senses.exampleCN: 她足够独立，能自己做决定。
senses.why: The stem depend means to hang from; the prefix in- says the hanging has been cut.
senses.whyCN: 词干 depend 意为「悬挂于」，前缀 in- 表示那根挂绳已被剪断。

senses.title: Not ruled by another country
senses.titleCN: 国家独立：不受他国统治
senses.definition: governing itself rather than being ruled from outside
senses.definitionCN: 自行治理而不受外部统治
senses.example: The island became independent in nineteen eighty.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛在一九八零年独立。
senses.why: Politics uses the same image at the scale of a whole territory.
senses.whyCN: 政治在整片领土的尺度上使用同一意象。

senses.title: Not connected or affected by
senses.definition: not depending on something else for its value or truth
senses.definitionCN: 其价值或真实性不取决于其他事物
senses.example: The two results are independent of each other.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个结果彼此无关。
senses.why: In mathematics and science, no hang means no link: one quantity does not move the other.
senses.whyCN: 在数学与科学里，不「挂」就是无关联：一个量不会带动另一个量。

senses.title: Not belonging to a party or company
senses.titleCN: 独立的：不属于党派或机构
senses.definition: not controlled by a political party, a company or a large organization
senses.definitionCN: 不受政党、公司或大型机构控制
senses.example: The report was written by an independent expert.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告由一位独立专家撰写。
senses.why: Freedom from an owner is valued as impartiality, so the word turns into a guarantee.
senses.whyCN: 摆脱所有者被视为公正，于是这个词本身成了一种保证。

senses.title: As a noun, one who is unaffiliated
senses.definition: a person who does not belong to a political party
senses.definitionCN: 不属于任何政党的人
senses.example: Two independents hold the balance in the council.
senses.exampleCN: 两名无党派人士在议会中掌握关键票数。
senses.why: A shorthand grew from the adjective: no party label, so simply an independent.
senses.whyCN: 从形容词缩出一个名词：没有党籍标签，就叫 independent。

intro.en: Independent joins in-, not, to dependent, from Latin dependere, to hang from.
intro.cn: independent 把否定前缀 in- 加到 dependent 之上，后者源自拉丁语 dependere「悬挂于」。

items.en: Pendere meant to hang, and dependere meant to hang down from something.
items.cn: pendere 意为「悬挂」，dependere 意为「从某物上垂挂」。

items.en: Ecclesiastical writers formed independentia for freedom from another's rule.
items.cn: 教会作家造出 independentia，表示不依附于他人统治。

items.en: The adjective entered English in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十七世纪进入英语。

items.en: Political and scientific uses made it a general word for no dependence.
items.cn: 政治与科学用法使它成为泛指「无依赖」的词。

items.en: The noun for an unaffiliated member of parliament appeared in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 指无党派议员的名词用法在十九世纪出现。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the pend- hang root; the near-meaning group holds words of acting alone.
note.cn: 形近组共用表示「悬挂」的 pend- 词根；近义组收表示独立行事的词。

entries.definition: The state of being free of control.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「独立」，是本词的名词形式。

entries.definition: Needing someone or something else.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「依赖的」，去掉 in- 即成。

entries.definition: A hanging ornament.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「吊坠」，同根。

entries.definition: Not joined to others.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「分开的、单独的」。

entries.definition: Working for oneself rather than an employer.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「自雇的」。

entries.definition: Not supporting either side.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「中立的」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the cut rope, the variant endings and the scientific sense of independence.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借剪断的绳子、词尾变化与科学里的独立。

normal.en: Depend plus in-, and the hanging rope is cut; nothing above holds you any more.
normal.cn: depend 加 in-，挂绳被剪断，上面再没有东西提着你。

normal.en: Independent of is the scientific spelling of no connection between two variables.
normal.cn: independent of 是科学里「两个变量无关联」的说法。

normal.en: The adjective ends in -ent, the noun in -ence: one letter keeps the family together.
normal.cn: 形容词以 -ent 结尾，名词以 -ence 结尾，一个字母维系着这家人。

normal.en: An independent voter stands between two columns, touching neither.
normal.cn: 独立选民站在两根柱子之间，谁也不扶。

normal.en: Independent films are made without a big studio hanging over the director.
normal.cn: 独立电影是在没有大制片厂压着导演的情况下拍出来的。

abstract.en: Independence is a relation described by its absence: freedom from someone, not freedom in general.
abstract.cn: 独立是一个由「缺席」描述的关系：相对于某人的自由，而非笼统的自由。

abstract.en: To be independent is to carry one's own weight, which is also to feel it.
abstract.cn: 独立就是自己承担重量，也就要感到那份重量。

abstract.en: Science charges a high price for independence: nothing may be taken on trust.
abstract.cn: 科学为独立付出高昂代价：任何事都不许只凭信任接受。

examples.en: The children grew more independent as they got older.
examples.cn: 孩子们长大后越来越独立。

examples.en: Her decision was independent of mine.
examples.cn: 她的决定与我无关。

examples.en: He works as an independent consultant.
examples.cn: 他做独立顾问。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印地盆登特」——自己印地、自己有盆，抬头登上高处，不靠别人。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ depend （de- + pendere「悬挂」）→ independent；同根词有 depend、dependence、suspend、pendant。

sensesIntro.en: Independent denies hanging from another, and the denial stretches from a person to a country, to a variable, to an organization and finally to a person without a party.
sensesIntro.cn: independent 否定「挂在别处」，这一否定从人扩展到国家、变量、机构，最后落成没有党籍的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two pillars standing without any beam between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：两根柱子各自立着，中间没有横梁。

branches.en: PERSON LINE: decisions are made without help.
branches.cn: 个人线：决定无需他人帮助。

branches.en: STATE LINE: a territory governs itself.
branches.cn: 国家线：领土自行治理。

branches.en: SCIENCE LINE: no variable moves another.
branches.cn: 科学线：没有变量牵动另一个。

branches.en: INSTITUTION LINE: no party or company owns the work.
branches.cn: 机构线：作品不属于党派或公司。

branches.en: POLITICS LINE: a label becomes a person.
branches.cn: 政治线：一个标签变成了一类人。

intro.en: A negative prefix on a compound of down and hang, plus an adjective ending.
intro.cn: 一个否定前缀加在「向下 + 悬挂」的合成词上，再接形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin pendere, to hang, with de-, down, and the negative in-, gave independentem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pendere「悬挂」加 de-「向下」，再加否定 in-，构成 independentem。

definition_zh: 表明；显示；指出；暗示
definition_en: to show that something exists or is likely, or to point it out
core_image: 手指在图纸上轻轻一点，示意某项出了问题
scene: 仪表盘上亮起红灯，说明发动机可能过热。The gauge indicates a sudden rise in temperature.
sceneCN: 这里 indicate 是「显示」（第 1 个义项：表明某种情况存在）；句意是仪表显示温度突然升高。

pos.zh: 动词：表明；显示；指出；暗示

derivatives.zh: 义为「迹象、指示」，由本词加 -ion 构成
义为「表明的、暗示的」，常与 of 连用
义为「索引、指标」，与本词同根

senses.title: To show as a sign
senses.titleCN: 表明：作为某种情况的标志
senses.definition: to show that a state or event exists
senses.definitionCN: 显示出某种状况或事件存在
senses.example: The gauge indicates a sudden rise in temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 仪表显示温度突然升高。
senses.why: The Latin dicare means to make known, and in- points the gesture at something specific.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 dicare 意为「使之知晓」，in- 则把这个动作指向具体对象。

senses.title: To point out directly
senses.definition: to show a thing to someone by pointing or naming it
senses.definitionCN: 通过指点或说出名称来把某物显示给人
senses.example: He indicated the seat beside him.
senses.exampleCN: 他指了指身边的座位。
senses.why: The oldest sense is physical: a finger makes the message known without words.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是具体的：一根手指不动嘴就把信息告知了。

senses.title: To suggest without saying
senses.definition: to make a wish or opinion known indirectly
senses.definitionCN: 间接地表露愿望或看法
senses.example: She indicated that she would rather stay.
senses.exampleCN: 她暗示自己宁可留下。
senses.why: A point can be polite as well as clear: the finger moves, the sentence remains unsaid.
senses.whyCN: 一指既可清晰也可含蓄：手指动了，话却没说出口。

senses.title: To be a sign of, of data
senses.titleCN: 表明：数据与研究中的用法
senses.definition: used of facts or studies to show what they suggest
senses.definitionCN: 用于事实或研究，表示其暗示的结论
senses.example: The results indicate that the method works.
senses.exampleCN: 结果表明这个方法有效。
senses.why: Research cannot speak, so the verb lets numbers point at a conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 研究本身不会说话，这个动词让数字指向一个结论。

senses.title: To signal on a vehicle
senses.titleCN: 打转向灯：车辆上的指示
senses.definition: to signal an intention to turn, using lights on a car
senses.definitionCN: 用汽车灯示意即将转向
senses.example: Always indicate before you turn.
senses.exampleCN: 转弯前一定要打转向灯。
senses.why: A machine repeats the gesture for you, so the word replaces the verb signal in British usage.
senses.whyCN: 机器代替人做这个手势，于是英式英语用这个词代替 signal。

intro.en: Indicate comes from Latin indicare, to point out, from in- and dicare, to make known.
intro.cn: indicate 来自拉丁语 indicare「指出」，由 in- 与 dicare「使之知晓」构成。

items.en: Dicare meant to proclaim or dedicate, from the same family as dicere, to say.
items.cn: dicare 意为宣告或奉献，与 dicere「说」同族。

items.en: Indicare meant to point out or show, often with a gesture.
items.cn: indicare 意为指出或显示，常伴手势。

items.en: English borrowed it to describe signs and measurements.
items.cn: 英语借它描述标志与测量结果。

items.en: The verb became a standard word in reports of data.
items.cn: 这个词成为报告数据时的标准用词。

items.en: British English made it the everyday word for signalling in a car.
items.cn: 英式英语让它成为汽车打转向灯的日常说法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the indic- root; the near-meaning group holds verbs of showing.
note.cn: 形近组共用 indic- 词根；近义组收表示「显示」的动词。

entries.definition: A sign that something exists.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「迹象、指示」。

entries.definition: A gauge or sign that shows a level.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「指示器、指标」。

entries.definition: To give time or effort to a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「奉献」，与 indicate 形近。

entries.definition: To make something visible or clear.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「显示」，最通用。

entries.definition: To make someone think something is likely.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「暗示、表明」，语气更弱。

entries.definition: To make known something hidden.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「揭示」，强调原本隐藏。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the pointing gesture, the dictionary root and the turn signal.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借指点的手势、dictionary 词根与转向灯。

normal.en: Dictionary and dictate share the root to say; indicate is the root plus in, saying towards a thing.
normal.cn: dictionary 与 dictate 共有「说」的词根；indicate 就是该词根加 in，朝着某物说话。

normal.en: Indicate that is the standard opening of any scientific finding.
normal.cn: indicate that 是一切科学结论的标准开头。

normal.en: Indicate the seat: a finger does the work of a whole sentence.
normal.cn: indicate the seat：一根手指干完了一整句话的活。

normal.en: In British cars, indicate is written on the turn signal lever's job description.
normal.cn: 在英国车里，转向灯杆的职责就用 indicate 来写。

normal.en: Indication, indicator, indicative: the ending changes but the pointing stays.
normal.cn: indication、indicator、indicative：词尾在变，指点的动作不变。

abstract.en: To indicate is to stay one step short of proof, and careful writers keep that step.
abstract.cn: 表明离证明还差一步，谨慎的写作者会守住这一步。

abstract.en: A sign is always smaller than the thing it points to.
abstract.cn: 标志永远比它所指向的东西小。

abstract.en: Language indicates before it states, and most arguments turn on that gap.
abstract.cn: 语言先暗示再陈述，多数争论就出在这道缝隙上。

examples.en: The map indicates where the river bends.
examples.cn: 地图标出了河流拐弯的地方。

examples.en: Early studies indicated a strong link.
examples.cn: 早期研究显示出很强的关联。

examples.en: He indicated with a nod that he agreed.
examples.cn: 他点头表示同意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印地开的」——地图印得清楚，标示该走的方向。

root: 拉丁语 in-（朝向）+ dicare（使之知晓，源自 dicere「说」）→ indicare（指出）；同根词有 index、indication、dedicate、dictate、dictionary。

sensesIntro.en: Indicate begins as a finger making a thing known, then covers any sign, indirect hints, research findings and finally a car's signal lamp.
sensesIntro.cn: indicate 起于手指把某物点明，随后涵盖任何标志、间接暗示、研究结论，最后还指汽车上的信号灯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger tapping a blueprint to show where the fault lies.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指在图纸上轻点，示出故障所在。

branches.en: SIGN LINE: readings and results point at a condition.
branches.cn: 标志线：读数与结果指向某种状况。

branches.en: GESTURE LINE: a hand shows the object itself.
branches.cn: 手势线：手直接示出对象。

branches.en: POLITENESS LINE: a wish is expressed without words.
branches.cn: 委婉线：愿望不必说出口。

branches.en: DATA LINE: numbers point at a conclusion.
branches.cn: 数据线：数字指向一个结论。

branches.en: MACHINE LINE: a lamp repeats the gesture for the driver.
branches.cn: 机器线：一盏灯替司机重复这个手势。

intro.en: A Latin prefix for pointing at, a root for making known, and a verb ending.
intro.cn: 一个表示「指向」的拉丁前缀、一个意为「使之知晓」的词根，以及一个动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin in-, upon, plus dicare, to make known, plus -are gave indicare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in-「朝向」加 dicare「使之知晓」加 -are，构成 indicare。

items.meaning: the act or sign of pointing

definition_zh: 迹象；指示；暗示
definition_en: a sign that shows something exists or is likely to happen
core_image: 树枝上刚冒出的那一点绿，说明春天要来了
scene: 医生看完化验单，说暂时没有恶化的迹象。There is no indication that the price will fall.
sceneCN: 这里 indication 是「迹象」（第 1 个义项：显示某事的标志）；句意是没有迹象表明价格会下跌。

pos.zh: 名词：迹象；指示；暗示

derivatives.zh: 义为「表明、显示」，是本词的动词来源
义为「指标、指示器」，同根名词

senses.title: A sign that something is so
senses.titleCN: 迹象：某情况存在的标志
senses.definition: a fact that shows something exists or is likely
senses.definitionCN: 显示某事存在或可能发生的事实
senses.example: There is no indication that the price will fall.
senses.exampleCN: 没有迹象表明价格会下跌。
senses.why: The noun turns the pointing act into the thing pointed at, so the finger becomes the trace it leaves.
senses.whyCN: 名词把「指」的动作转为「被指着的东西」，手指变成了它留下的痕迹。

senses.title: A signal given to someone
senses.definition: a signal or piece of information given on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 有意发出的信号或信息
senses.example: He gave a slight indication with his hand.
senses.exampleCN: 他用手轻轻示意了一下。
senses.why: A deliberate point is meant to be read, so the noun also names the signal itself.
senses.whyCN: 刻意的指点就是给人读的，于是名词也指那个信号本身。

senses.title: A hint about future action
senses.titleCN: 暗示：对未来打算的透露
senses.definition: a hint that something will be done, often without a promise
senses.definitionCN: 对即将做某事的暗示，通常不作承诺
senses.example: There were indications of an early election.
senses.exampleCN: 有一些提前大选的暗示。
senses.why: Politics works by hints, and the word keeps the door open because a sign is not a promise.
senses.whyCN: 政治靠暗示运转，而这个词留有余地，因为迹象不等于承诺。

senses.title: In medicine, a symptom pointing to treatment
senses.titleCN: 适应症：医学上指指向治疗的症状
senses.definition: a condition for which a particular medicine or treatment is suitable
senses.definitionCN: 某种药物或治疗适用的状况
senses.example: The drug has few indications in children.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药在儿童身上可用的适应症很少。
senses.why: A symptom points at a remedy, and doctors borrowed the same pointing word.
senses.whyCN: 症状指向一种疗法，医生借用了同样这枚「指」字。

intro.en: Indication is the noun from Latin indicare, to point out, formed with the suffix -ation.
intro.cn: indication 是拉丁语 indicare「指出」加 -ation 词尾构成的名词。

items.en: Indicatio named the act of showing or the price named in a sale.
items.cn: indicatio 指显示的动作，也指买卖中报出的价格。

items.en: English used it for signs that reveal a hidden state.
items.cn: 英语用它表示揭示隐藏状况的标志。

items.en: Medical writing adopted it for the conditions a drug treats.
items.cn: 医学写作采用它指药物可治疗的状况。

items.en: In news writing it became a cautious word for possible events.
items.cn: 新闻写作中它成为对可能事件的谨慎措辞。

items.en: The phrase indication of is now commoner than any single strong claim.
items.cn: 如今 indication of 这种说法比任何强断言都常见。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the indic- root; the near-meaning group holds words for signs and hints.
note.cn: 形近组共用 indic- 词根；近义组收表示迹象与暗示的词。

entries.definition: To show or point out something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「表明」，是本词的动词形式。

entries.definition: A gauge or measure that shows a level.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「指标、指示器」。

entries.definition: Hard work given to a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「奉献、专心」，与 indication 形近。

entries.definition: Something that shows something else exists.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「迹象、标志」。

entries.definition: A small indirect suggestion.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「暗示」，更轻微。

entries.definition: A piece of information that helps solve a problem.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「线索」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the first green bud, the noun suffix and the cautious phrasing of news.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借第一点新绿、名词词尾与新闻里的谨慎措辞。

normal.en: Indicate plus -ion: the act of pointing becomes a thing that was pointed at.
normal.cn: indicate 加 -ion：指的动作变成了被指出的东西。

normal.en: The bud on a bare branch is an indication of spring, not spring itself.
normal.cn: 光秃枝头的芽是春天的迹象，而不是春天本身。

normal.en: There is no indication that is the politest way to say nothing has happened yet.
normal.cn: there is no indication that 是「暂时什么也没发生」最客气的说法。

normal.en: A hint is an indication given on purpose; a clue is one you happen to find.
normal.cn: hint 是有意给出的暗示，clue 是偶然找到的线索。

normal.en: Prescription labels list indications: the conditions the drug is meant to treat.
normal.cn: 处方说明上列着适应症，即这药要治的状况。

abstract.en: An indication is a bridge built halfway, enough to cross if someone else builds the rest.
abstract.cn: 迹象是一座修了一半的桥，别人补完剩下的一段才能过。

abstract.en: Signs do not lie, but readers of signs often do.
abstract.cn: 迹象不说谎，读迹象的人却常常说谎。

abstract.en: To ask for indications is to admit that certainty has not arrived.
abstract.cn: 要求给出迹象，等于承认确定性还没到。

examples.en: The results give a clear indication of progress.
examples.cn: 结果明确显示了进展的迹象。

examples.en: There was every indication that he would win.
examples.cn: 种种迹象都表明他会赢。

examples.en: Her silence was an indication of disagreement.
examples.cn: 她的沉默是不同意的表示。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印地开的省」——书上印着开列的事项，那是迹象与提示。

root: 拉丁语 in-（朝向）+ dicare（使之知晓）+ -ation（名词词尾）→ indicatio（指示）；同根词有 indicate、predict、contradict。

sensesIntro.en: Indication turns the act of pointing into the evidence left behind, then into a signal, a hint and finally a medical condition that points at a remedy.
sensesIntro.cn: indication 把「指」的动作变成留下的证据，再变成信号、暗示，最后成为指向疗法的医学适应症。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first green bud on a bare branch.
core.cn: 核心意象：光秃枝头冒出的第一点绿。

branches.en: EVIDENCE LINE: a fact points at a hidden state.
branches.cn: 证据线：事实指向隐藏的状况。

branches.en: SIGNAL LINE: a gesture is meant to be read.
branches.cn: 信号线：手势本来就是给人读的。

branches.en: POLITICS LINE: hints leave the future open.
branches.cn: 政治线：暗示让未来留有余地。

branches.en: MEDICINE LINE: a symptom points at a remedy.
branches.cn: 医学线：症状指向一种疗法。

branches.en: RHETORIC LINE: it reports without promising.
branches.cn: 修辞线：它只报告，不作承诺。

intro.en: A prefix for pointing at, a root for making known, and a noun ending for an action.
intro.cn: 一个表示「指向」的前缀、一个意为「使之知晓」的词根，以及表示动作的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin indicare, to point out, with -ationem, gave indicatio, a showing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 indicare「指出」加 -ationem，构成 indicatio「显示」。

items.meaning: having the nature of a sign
